source.classical: James Legge (trans.), The Yi King, Sacred Books of the East vol. 16 (Oxford, 1882; 2nd ed. 1899). Public domain. Text via the Internet Sacred Text Archive.
source.modern: Plain-English interpretations, practical guidance and Jungian notes written for I Ching — The Living Oracle (MIT/CC BY 4.0).

trigrams.name: Qián
trigrams.text: Three solid lines: pure yang. Qián is the energy of heaven, tireless, creative and initiating. It stands for strength, leadership and persistence.

trigrams.name: Kūn
trigrams.text: Three broken lines: pure yin. Kūn is the earth that receives, supports and nourishes everything. It stands for devotion, patience and care.

trigrams.name: Zhèn
trigrams.text: One solid line beneath two broken lines: energy bursting up from below. Zhèn is thunder, shock and the first stirring of new life in spring.

trigrams.name: Xùn
trigrams.text: One broken line beneath two solid lines. Xùn is wind and the roots of trees: gentle influence that penetrates everywhere through persistence.

trigrams.name: Kǎn
trigrams.text: A solid line held between two broken lines, like water flowing in a ravine. Kǎn is danger and depth, but also sincerity and the courage to keep flowing.

trigrams.name: Lí
trigrams.text: A broken line held between two solid lines: an empty center that shines. Lí is fire and light, clarity and awareness, which must cling to something to burn.

trigrams.name: Gèn
trigrams.text: One solid line resting on two broken lines, like a mountain on the earth. Gèn is stillness, meditation and knowing when to stop.

trigrams.name: Duì
trigrams.text: One broken line above two solid lines, like the open surface of a lake. Duì is joy, conversation and the pleasure of sharing.

hexagrams.name: The Creative
hexagrams.core: a time of strong creative energy, when steady, principled effort can start something important
hexagrams.now: You are in a period of strong, active energy. Something wants to begin, grow or take shape through you, and you have more power to influence events than you may think. The Creative is pure strength: heaven moving without pause. Its traditional words promise great success, but only to effort that stays correct and persistent. The key is not force for its own sake but strength that keeps going, day after day, in the right direction. Notice where your energy naturally wants to go, and ask whether your ambition serves something worthwhile.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward more initiative and momentum. Energy that was held back is ready to act, and steady, principled effort is likely to carry further than hesitation.
do: Commit to a clear direction and work at it consistently
Match your timing to the moment, waiting when the time is early and acting when it is ripe
Lead by example rather than by pressure
avoid: Pushing past healthy limits out of pride
Using strength to dominate other people
hexagrams.love: Bring warmth and initiative, but let your partner meet you halfway; strength in a relationship means reliability, not control.
hexagrams.work: A good time to start or lead a project. Set a clear goal, keep a steady pace and earn trust through consistent results.
hexagrams.self: Your energy is high. Channel it into a discipline you can sustain, rather than bursts of effort followed by exhaustion.
hexagrams.jung: The Creative can mirror the archetype of the active, conscious will, sometimes pictured as the hero or the sun. Ask whether you are identifying too strongly with your own power. Jung warned that inflation, the sense of being larger than life, often comes just before a fall, which the sixth line's arrogant dragon also describes.
hexagrams.example: Someone starting a business, a training plan or a creative project who needs to keep showing up every day, while knowing when to pause.
hexagrams.judgment: Khien (represents) what is great and originating, penetrating, advantageous, correct and firm.
hexagrams.image: Heaven, in its motion, (gives the idea of) strength. The superior man, in accordance with this, nerves himself to ceaseless activity.

lines.legge: In the first (or lowest) NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon lying hid (in the deep). It is not the time for active doing.
lines.plain: The dragon is still hidden under the water. Your abilities are real but not yet ready to be shown. This is a time for preparation, not action. Keep developing quietly and do not force an early start.

lines.legge: In the second NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon appearing in the field. It will be advantageous to meet with the great man.
lines.plain: The dragon appears in the field. Your potential is becoming visible. Seek out people with experience and influence; a good mentor or ally can help you grow now.

lines.legge: In the third NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the superior man active and vigilant all the day, and in the evening still careful and apprehensive. (The position is) dangerous, but there will be no mistake.
lines.plain: You are working hard all day and still alert at night. The position is demanding and carries some danger, but steady care keeps you from mistakes. Stay diligent without letting worry consume you.

lines.legge: In the fourth NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as the dragon looking) as if he were leaping up, but still in the deep. There will be no mistake.
lines.plain: The dragon seems ready to leap, yet is still in the deep water. You stand at a threshold and can choose to rise or wait. Either choice can be right if it is made honestly; there is no blame.

lines.legge: In the fifth NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon on the wing in the sky. It will be advantageous to meet with the great man.
lines.plain: The dragon flies in the sky. You are at the height of your power and influence. Use it well, and stay connected with capable and wise people.

lines.legge: In the sixth (or topmost) NINE, undivided, (we see its subject as) the dragon exceeding the proper limits. There will be occasion for repentance.
lines.plain: The dragon has gone too high and exceeded its limits. Pride and overreach lead to regret. Step back before strength turns into arrogance.

allLines.legge: (The lines of this hexagram are all strong and undivided, as appears from) the use of the number NINE. If the host of dragons (thus) appearing were to divest themselves of their heads, there would be good fortune.
allLines.plain: When all six lines change, a host of dragons appears with no one at their head. Strength that does not insist on being first brings good fortune: lead through cooperation, not domination.

hexagrams.name: The Receptive
hexagrams.core: a time to be receptive, supportive and patient, letting things grow rather than forcing them
hexagrams.now: This is a time for receptivity rather than initiative. Like the earth that receives seed and quietly supports all growth, you may achieve the most by responding, supporting and following a sound lead rather than trying to control the situation. Legge's text says that if the superior person takes the lead he goes astray, but if he follows he finds his way. Receptive does not mean passive: it means steady, dependable and open, like the "firmness of a mare" that keeps going without fighting the rider. Look for what your situation needs from you, then give it patiently.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a quieter, more receptive phase, where patience, cooperation and support achieve more than personal initiative.
do: Listen carefully and respond to what is actually needed
Support people and projects that deserve it
let results grow in their own time
hexagrams.love: Listen more than you speak and show care through consistent, practical support. Do not try to steer everything.
hexagrams.work: Support a strong leader or plan rather than competing for control. Thorough, reliable work will be noticed.
hexagrams.self: Practise acceptance. Not everything needs to be fixed by effort; some things need room to grow.
hexagrams.jung: The Receptive is often linked with the archetypal feminine, the mother and the earth: the capacity to receive, hold and nourish. Psychologically it can invite you to listen to the unconscious rather than to command it. Dreams, feelings and quiet intuitions may carry guidance now.
hexagrams.example: A new team member who learns the system before proposing changes, or a parent who supports a child's interests instead of directing them.
hexagrams.judgment: Khwăn (represents) what is great and originating, penetrating, advantageous, correct and having the firmness of a mare. When the superior man (here intended) has to make any movement, if he take the initiative, he will go astray; if he follow, he will find his (proper) lord. The advantageousness will be seen in his getting friends in the south-west, and losing friends in the north-east. If he rest in correctness and firmness, there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.image: The (capacity and sustaining) power of the earth is what is denoted by Khwăn. The superior man, in accordance with this, with his large virtue supports (men and) things.

lines.legge: In the first SIX, divided, (we see its subject) treading on hoarfrost. The strong ice will come (by and by).
lines.plain: Frost underfoot means hard ice will follow. Small signs show where things are heading. Pay attention to early warnings and deal with problems while they are still small.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, (shows the attribute of) being straight, square, and great. (Its operation), without repeated efforts, will be in every respect advantageous.
lines.plain: Straight, square and great: honest, natural action succeeds without strain. You do not need elaborate effort; acting from your true nature is enough.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, (shows its subject) keeping his excellence under restraint, but firmly maintaining it. If he should have occasion to engage in the king's service, though he will not claim the success (for himself), he will bring affairs to a good issue.
lines.plain: You keep your talents hidden but remain steady. If you serve a larger cause, do not claim credit; your work will still bring things to a good end.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, (shows the symbol of) a sack tied up. There will be no ground for blame or for praise.
lines.plain: A tied-up sack: be discreet and keep your counsel. Staying quiet earns neither blame nor praise, and that is what this moment requires.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, (shows) the yellow lower garment. There will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: The yellow lower garment, a symbol of modesty and the middle way. Quiet dignity and reliable service bring great good fortune.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided (shows) dragons fighting in the wild. Their blood is purple and yellow.
lines.plain: Dragons fight in the wild and their blood is spilled. When the receptive tries to compete with the creative, both are hurt. Avoid a power struggle that has gone too far.

allLines.legge: (The lines of this hexagram are all weak and divided, as appears from) the use of the number six. If those (who are thus represented) be perpetually correct and firm, advantage will arise.
allLines.plain: When all six lines change, the text advises lasting firmness and correctness. Receptivity should be steady and sincere over the long term; constancy turns yielding into strength.

hexagrams.name: Difficulty at the Beginning
hexagrams.core: the messy, difficult start of something new, which succeeds with patience, structure and help
hexagrams.now: You may be at the beginning of something new, and beginnings are rarely tidy. The hexagram shows a seedling pushing up through hard ground, or clouds and thunder before a storm clears the air. There is great potential and real chaos at the same time. Legge's text promises great progress, but warns against rushing forward and advises "appointing feudal princes" — finding helpers and creating structure. Confusion now is a natural stage of growth, not a sign of failure. Organize what you can, ask for help and do not give up.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a new beginning, with the usual confusion of early growth. It will need patience, structure and support from others.
do: Break the situation into small, manageable steps
Ask for help and gather allies
Persist calmly through the early confusion
avoid: Giving up because the start is difficult
hexagrams.love: A new or renewed relationship may feel uncertain. Go slowly, communicate clearly and do not judge its future by its awkward start.
hexagrams.work: New ventures face growing pains. Put basic structures in place and recruit good helpers before expanding.
hexagrams.self: Accept that learning something new feels clumsy. Confusion is the doorway to growth.
hexagrams.jung: Psychologically this can describe the birth of something new from the unconscious, a new attitude or creative idea struggling into consciousness. Such births are often accompanied by anxiety and disorder. Hold the tension rather than suppressing the new impulse.
hexagrams.example: The first months of a new job, a move to a new city, or launching a project before routines are established.
hexagrams.judgment: Kun (indicates that in the case which it presupposes) there will be great progress and success, and the advantage will come from being correct and firm. (But) any movement in advance should not be (lightly) undertaken. There will be advantage in appointing feudal princes.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) clouds and (that representing) thunder form Kun. The superior man, in accordance with this, (adjusts his measures of government) as in sorting the threads of the warp and woof.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows the difficulty (its subject has) in advancing. It will be advantageous for him to abide correct and firm; advantageous (also) to be made a feudal ruler.
lines.plain: Difficulty in moving forward. Stay firm and correct, and gather helpers. Hesitation at this stage is wise; build your base before you advance.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows (its subject) distressed and obliged to return; (even) the horses of her chariot (also) seem to be retreating. (But) not by a spoiler (is she assailed), but by one who seeks her to be his wife. The young lady maintains her firm correctness, and declines a union. After ten years she will be united, and have children.
lines.plain: Progress stalls and you feel turned back. An offer comes that is not what it seems, or not yet right. Stay true to yourself; the right union will come in time, even if it takes long.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows one following the deer without (the guidance of) the forester, and only finding himself in the midst of the forest. The superior man, acquainted with the secret risks, thinks it better to give up the chase. If he went forward, he would regret it.
lines.plain: Chasing a deer without a guide leads only deeper into the forest. Going on alone and unprepared will bring regret. The wise choice is to stop.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows (its subject as a lady), the horses of whose chariot appear in retreat. She seeks, however, (the help of) him who seeks her to be his wife. Advance will be fortunate; all will turn out advantageously.
lines.plain: Now is the time to seek a partner or helper. Accept the connection that is offered; moving forward together brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the difficulties in the way of (its subject's) dispensing the rich favours that might be expected from him. With firmness and correctness there will be good fortune in small things; (even) with them in great things there will be evil.
lines.plain: You have resources to give, but conditions limit how much you can do. Be careful in small matters; trying to accomplish too much at once would be unwise.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows (its subject) with the horses of his chariot obliged to retreat, and weeping tears of blood in streams.
lines.plain: Tears of blood flow as the horses turn back. Despair at the difficulty of the beginning. Grief should not last forever; change your approach rather than staying stuck.

hexagrams.name: Youthful Folly
hexagrams.core: a time of inexperience, when sincere learning and good guidance matter more than pretending to know
hexagrams.now: This hexagram is about learning. Someone is inexperienced, perhaps you, perhaps someone you are guiding. The image is a spring flowing at the foot of a mountain: fresh water that does not yet know its way. The traditional text says the teacher does not seek the student; the student must come sincerely. It also notes that asking the same question again and again is disrespectful — a pointed reminder about re-consulting the oracle. Approach the situation with an open, teachable mind, and be honest about what you do not yet know.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a learning phase. You may need to seek knowledge, accept guidance or admit what you do not yet understand.
do: Ask sincerely for guidance and then act on it
Admit what you do not know
Learn step by step, with patience
avoid: Asking the same question repeatedly hoping for a different answer
Pretending to know more than you do
hexagrams.love: Be honest about your inexperience or confusion. Learn about your partner rather than assuming you already understand.
hexagrams.work: Seek training or a mentor. If you are leading, teach patiently but set clear boundaries.
hexagrams.self: Curiosity is your best ally now. Treat confusion as the beginning of understanding.
hexagrams.jung: Youthful Folly can mirror the archetype of the puer or child: fresh, open but naive. It may also point to the relationship between ego and inner wisdom. The ego must approach the deeper Self sincerely, not demand instant answers.
hexagrams.example: A student facing a difficult subject, a new parent learning on the job, or someone repeatedly asking for advice they never follow.
hexagrams.judgment: Măng (indicates that in the case which it presupposes) there will be progress and success. I do not (go and) seek the youthful and inexperienced, but he comes and seeks me. When he shows (the sincerity that marks) the first recourse to divination, I instruct him. If he apply a second and third time, that is troublesome; and I do not instruct the troublesome. There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and beneath it that for a spring issuing forth form Măng. The superior man, in accordance with this, strives to be resolute in his conduct and nourishes his virtue.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, (has respect to) the dispelling of ignorance. It will be advantageous to use punishment (for that purpose), and to remove the shackles (from the mind). But going on in that way (of punishment) will give occasion for regret.
lines.plain: To dispel ignorance, discipline can help, but punishment should not become a habit. Use firm structure to start learning, then loosen it.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) exercising forbearance with the ignorant, in which there will be good fortune; and admitting (even the goodness of women, which will also be fortunate. (He may be described also as) a son able to (sustain the burden of) his family.
lines.plain: Bear patiently with the inexperienced, and even accept help from unexpected people. Like a son able to carry the family, you can take responsibility well.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, (seems to say) that one should not marry a woman whose emblem it might be, for that, when she sees a man of wealth, she will not keep her person from him, and in no wise will advantage come from her.
lines.plain: Do not commit to someone who abandons themselves at the sight of wealth or advantage. Avoid relationships or choices based on mere attraction to power or money.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, (shows its subject as if) bound in chains of ignorance. There will be occasion for regret.
lines.plain: Bound by ignorance and isolation. Cutting yourself off from good guidance leads to regret. Seek out people who can help.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject as a simple lad without experience. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The innocent, childlike learner meets good fortune. Humility and openness make you easy to teach.

lines.legge: In the topmost NINE, undivided, we see one smiting the ignorant (youth). But no advantage will come from doing him an injury. Advantage would come from warding off injury from him.
lines.plain: Correcting folly: discipline is needed, but do not attack. Protect against harm rather than inflicting it.

hexagrams.name: Waiting
hexagrams.core: a time of waiting for the right moment, using the pause to prepare and stay nourished
hexagrams.now: You are being asked to wait — not anxiously, but with confidence and readiness. The image is clouds rising in the sky: rain will come, but it cannot be forced. The traditional text links sincerity with brilliant success and says it will be advantageous to cross the great water — that is, to undertake something important, once the time is right. Waiting here is active. Take care of your health and relationships, gather information and prepare, so that when the moment arrives you are ready to move.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a period of waiting, when the most effective thing is to prepare calmly and trust that the right time will come.
do: Use the waiting time to prepare and gather strength
Keep up good habits and look after your wellbeing
avoid: Forcing a decision before conditions are ready
Letting worry turn waiting into suffering
hexagrams.love: Do not push for answers or commitments right now. Enjoy what is good in the present and let trust develop.
hexagrams.work: Prepare thoroughly, but wait for the right opening rather than forcing a launch or confrontation.
hexagrams.self: Practise patience as a skill. Rest, nourishment and calm are productive now.
hexagrams.jung: Waiting invites you to tolerate uncertainty without escaping into anxious action. Psychologically, insight often matures beneath the surface before it can be acted on. The ego's impatience is set against the slower rhythm of the unconscious.
hexagrams.example: Waiting for exam results, a job offer or a medical recovery, and choosing to rest and prepare instead of worrying.
hexagrams.judgment: Hsü intimates that, with the sincerity which is declared in it, there will be brilliant success. With firmness there will be good fortune; and it will be advantageous to cross the great stream.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram for) clouds ascending over that for the sky forms Hsü. The superior man, in accordance with this, eats and drinks, feasts and enjoys himself (as if there were nothing else to employ him).

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject waiting in the distant border. It will be well for him constantly to maintain (the purpose thus shown), in which case there will be no error.
lines.plain: Waiting in the open meadow, far from danger. Keep up your normal routine and remain steady; there is no mistake.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject waiting on the sand (of the mountain stream). He will (suffer) the small (injury of) being spoken (against), but in the end there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Waiting on the sand, closer to trouble. There may be some gossip or criticism, but in the end things turn out well.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject in the mud (close by the stream). He thereby invites the approach of injury.
lines.plain: Waiting in the mud invites trouble. You have moved too close to danger. Be careful and avoid making things worse.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject waiting in (the place of) blood. But he will get out of the cavern.
lines.plain: Waiting in blood: you are in a dangerous situation. Stay calm and get out of the hole; you will escape.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject waiting amidst the appliances of a feast. Through his firmness and correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Waiting with wine and food. Even in difficult times, enjoy the nourishment available and keep steady. Firm correctness brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject entered into the cavern. (But) there are three guests coming, without being urged, (to his help). If he receive them respectfully, there will be good fortune in the end.
lines.plain: You fall into the pit, but three unexpected guests arrive. Receive them respectfully, even if they are not what you expected; help can come from surprising sources.

hexagrams.name: Conflict
hexagrams.core: a conflict in which fairness, restraint and impartial help matter more than winning
hexagrams.now: This hexagram shows a conflict: heaven rising upward and water flowing down, moving apart. You may be in a dispute, or feel inner tension between what you want and what is possible. The traditional text says that even if you are sincere and in the right, you meet obstruction. Stopping halfway brings good fortune; pushing the conflict to the bitter end brings misfortune. Seeking a wise mediator helps. Before acting, ask whether you are clear about your goal, and whether winning would really be worth the cost.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a point of tension or disagreement. It will be important to handle conflict fairly and to know when to stop.
do: Clarify the facts and your real goals before arguing
Seek a fair mediator or neutral advice
avoid: Starting major new ventures while a dispute is unresolved
hexagrams.love: Do not try to win the argument at all costs. Look for what each of you really needs and accept a fair middle ground.
hexagrams.work: Resolve disputes through clear agreements and neutral help. Get commitments in writing before starting new projects.
hexagrams.self: Inner conflict may mean two of your values are pulling against each other. Name both sides honestly before choosing.
hexagrams.jung: Conflict can represent a clash between opposites within the psyche, such as ego and shadow or duty and desire. Jung believed that holding the tension of opposites, rather than letting one side simply win, can lead to a new third position.
hexagrams.example: A dispute with a neighbour, a business partner or a family member, where a fair compromise is wiser than a long legal battle.
hexagrams.judgment: Sung intimates how, though there is sincerity in one's contention, he will yet meet with opposition and obstruction; but if he cherish an apprehensive caution, there will be good fortune, while, if he must prosecute the contention to the (bitter) end, there will be evil. It will be advantageous to see the great man; it will not be advantageous to cross the great stream.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) heaven and (that representing) water, moving away from each other, form Sung. The superior man, in accordance with this, in the transaction of affairs takes good counsel about his first steps.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject not perpetuating the matter about which (the contention is). He will suffer the small (injury) of being spoken against, but the end will be fortunate.
lines.plain: Do not drag out the conflict. There may be a little criticism, but ending it early brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject unequal to the contention. If he retire and keep concealed (where) the inhabitants of his city are (only) three hundred families, he will fall into no mistake.
lines.plain: You cannot win this fight. Retreat home and keep quiet; the people around you will be spared harm.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping in the old place assigned for his support, and firmly correct. Perilous as the position is, there will be good fortune in the end. Should he perchance engage in the king's business, he will not (claim the merit of) achievement.
lines.plain: Live on what you have honestly earned and stay correct. Danger exists, but you will come through. If you serve someone else, do not claim the success.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject unequal to the contention. He returns to (the study of Heaven's) ordinances, changes (his wish to contend), and rests in being firm and correct. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: You cannot win, so you turn back and accept what is right. Changing your attitude and settling down brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject contending;--and with great good fortune.
lines.plain: Bringing your case before a fair and just authority. Contention handled with integrity brings great good fortune.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows how its subject may have the leathern belt conferred on him (by the sovereign), and thrice it shall be taken from him in a morning.
lines.plain: Even if you win honors through fighting, they may be taken away three times in a single morning. Victory gained through conflict is unstable.

hexagrams.name: The Army
hexagrams.core: a time for disciplined, organized collective effort under responsible leadership
hexagrams.now: The Army is about organized collective effort. The image is water hidden in the earth: a great force held within an orderly structure. Whatever you face may require discipline, coordination and a leader whom people trust — perhaps you. The traditional text says success depends on a mature, experienced leader and on a just cause. Clear roles, clear rules and a worthy purpose are essential. This is not about aggression; it is about bringing scattered energies under responsible direction.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a need for organization and discipline. Collective efforts will need clear leadership and a just purpose.
do: Choose experienced leaders and trust them
Keep your purpose just and your methods disciplined
avoid: Giving responsibility to inexperienced or self-serving people
hexagrams.love: Shared goals and fair roles strengthen a relationship. Work as a team, not as competitors.
hexagrams.work: Organize the team, clarify who decides what, and keep standards high. Discipline now prevents chaos later.
hexagrams.self: Bring order to your habits and priorities. Inner discipline gives your energy a direction.
hexagrams.jung: The Army can symbolize the organization of many inner drives under a central purpose. Psychologically, the question is who is in command: a mature, integrated center, or a fragmentary complex that has taken over.
hexagrams.example: Organizing a community project, leading a sports team, or coordinating family members during a crisis.
hexagrams.judgment: Sze indicates how, in the case which it supposes, with firmness and correctness, and (a leader of) age and experience, there will be good fortune and no error.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the earth and in the midst of it that representing water, form Sze. The superior man, in accordance with this, nourishes and educates the people, and collects (from among them) the multitudes (of the hosts).

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows the host going forth according to the rules (for such a movement). If these be not good, there will be evil.
lines.plain: An army must set out in proper order. Without discipline, even a good cause will end badly.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows (the leader) in the midst of the host. There will be good fortune and no error. The king has thrice conveyed to him the orders (of his favour).
lines.plain: The leader is in the midst of the army, trusted and supported. There is good fortune; recognition comes three times.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows how the host may, possibly, have many inefficient leaders. There will be evil.
lines.plain: The army carries corpses in its wagons. Divided leadership or incompetence brings misfortune.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows the host in retreat. There is no error.
lines.plain: The army retreats. Withdrawing at the right time is no mistake.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows birds in the fields, which it will be advantageous to seize (and destroy). In that case there will be no error. If the oldest son leads the host, and younger men (idly occupy offices assigned to them), however firm and correct he may be, there will be evil.
lines.plain: There is game in the field; it is right to act against it. Let the experienced elder lead; if inexperienced people take charge, misfortune follows.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows the great ruler delivering his charges, (appointing some) to be rulers of states, and others to undertake the headship of clans; but small men should not be employed (in such positions).
lines.plain: The great ruler gives out rewards and founds states. Do not give power to petty or unworthy people, even after success.

hexagrams.name: Holding Together
hexagrams.core: a time of joining together around a trustworthy center, where sincerity and good timing build lasting bonds
hexagrams.now: Holding Together is about union. Water on the earth flows together naturally, finding its level and joining with other water. You may be seeking or forming connections — with a group, a partner, a community or a cause. The traditional text advises you to examine yourself: are you worthy to be a center that others gather around, or are you joining the right center? It also warns that those who hesitate too long arrive late and miss out. Sincere, timely commitment brings good fortune.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward union and belonging. It will be important to join the right people sincerely and without hesitation.
do: Examine whether your commitments are sincere and well-chosen
Join or build a community around shared values
Act in good time rather than waiting until the chance is gone
avoid: Joining the wrong group out of loneliness
Hesitating so long that the opportunity passes
hexagrams.love: Commitment and sincerity matter now. If the relationship is right, show it; if you are unsure, look honestly at why.
hexagrams.work: Build alliances and partnerships based on trust. A good team leader draws people together naturally.
hexagrams.self: Ask where you truly belong. Your loyalties shape who you become.
hexagrams.jung: Holding Together reflects the human need for belonging and the psychological task of finding a central value around which the personality can unite. Jung called this center the Self.
hexagrams.example: Joining a club, committing to a partnership, or bringing a divided team together around a shared goal.
hexagrams.judgment: Pî indicates that (under the conditions which it supposes) there is good fortune. But let (the principal party intended in it) re-examine himself, (as if) by divination, whether his virtue be great, unintermitting, and firm. If it be so, there will be no error. Those who have not rest will then come to him; and with those who are (too) late in coming it will be ill.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the earth, and over it (that representing) water, form Pî. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, established the various states and maintained an affectionate relation to their princes.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject seeking by his sincerity to win the attachment of his object. There will be no error. Let (the breast) be full of sincerity as an earthenware vessel is of its contents, and it will in the end bring other advantages.
lines.plain: Hold to others with sincerity, as full as an earthen jug. Sincerity attracts unexpected good fortune.

lines.legge: In the second SIX, divided, we see the movement towards union and attachment proceeding from the inward (mind). With firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Union comes from within. Stay true to your inner commitments; firmness brings good fortune.

lines.legge: In the third SIX, divided, we see its subject seeking for union with such as ought not to be associated with.
lines.plain: You are seeking union with the wrong people. Be careful of associations that do not share your values.

lines.legge: In the fourth SIX, divided, we see its subject seeking for union with the one beyond himself. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Show your loyalty openly to someone worthy. Firm, outward commitment brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, affords the most illustrious instance of seeking union and attachment. (We seem to see in it) the king urging his pursuit of the game (only) in three directions, and allowing the escape of all the animals before him, while the people of his towns do not warn one another (to prevent it). There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The king hunts on three sides and lets the game escape on the fourth. Union is offered freely, not forced. Let people come of their own accord; this brings good fortune.

lines.legge: In the topmost SIX, divided, we see one seeking union and attachment without having taken the first step (to such an end). There will be evil.
lines.plain: Seeking union without a head, too late, without a true beginning. This leads to misfortune.

hexagrams.name: Small Taming
hexagrams.alt: The Taming Power of the Small
hexagrams.core: a time when small, gentle influences restrain great energy, and progress comes through patience and detail
hexagrams.now: Dense clouds gather but no rain falls yet. Your energy or plans are being held back by circumstances that are small but persistent. You cannot force a breakthrough now, but gentle, steady influence can shape what happens next. Small Taming asks you to refine details, improve your approach and build up resources. Like wind slowly shaping the sky, gentleness and persistence achieve what force cannot. The rain — the release — will come when enough has accumulated.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase of gentle restraint, when small adjustments and patience achieve more than big moves.
do: Focus on details and small improvements
Use gentle persuasion rather than force
Save energy and resources for later
avoid: Trying to force a big breakthrough now
hexagrams.love: Small kindnesses matter more than grand gestures right now. Be patient with differences.
hexagrams.work: Refine your plans and polish the details. A major launch may need to wait until conditions improve.
hexagrams.self: Build habits in small increments. Gentle consistency will add up.
hexagrams.jung: Small Taming can symbolize the way a small but persistent attitude, such as a gentle feeling or quiet value, can restrain a powerful drive. The psyche is not changed by force but by repeated, patient attention.
hexagrams.example: Saving a little money every month, gradually persuading a skeptical colleague, or slowly recovering from an injury.
hexagrams.judgment: Hsiâo Khû indicates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and success. (We see) dense clouds, but no rain coming from our borders in the west.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the sky, and that representing wind moving above it, form Hsiâo Khû The superior man, in accordance with this, adorns the outward manifestation of his virtue.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject returning and pursuing his own course. What mistake should he fall into? There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Return to your own path. You have not gone wrong; going back to what is right brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject, by the attraction (of the former line), returning (to the proper course). There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: You are drawn back to the right way along with others. Returning together brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of a carriage, the strap beneath which has been removed, or of a husband and wife looking on each other with averted eyes.
lines.plain: The spokes come off the cart; husband and wife roll their eyes at each other. Conflict arises when you push against restraint. Do not force the issue.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity. The danger of bloodshed is thereby averted, and his (ground for) apprehension dismissed. There will be no mistake.
lines.plain: If you are sincere, worry departs and danger is avoided. Honest intentions protect you.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity, and drawing others to unite with him. Rich in resources, he employs his neighbours (in the same cause with himself).
lines.plain: Sincerity binds people together, and shared wealth with neighbours. Loyalty creates mutual benefit.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows how the rain has fallen, and the (onward progress) is stayed;--(so) must we value the full accumulation of the virtue (represented by the upper trigram). But a wife (exercising restraint), however firm and correct she may be, is in a position of peril, (and like) the moon approaching to the full. If the superior man prosecute his measures (in such circumstances), there will be evil.
lines.plain: The rain has come and there is rest. Accumulated virtue has borne fruit. But do not push further: the moon is nearly full, and persistence now brings danger.

hexagrams.name: Treading
hexagrams.core: a delicate situation, like stepping on the tail of a tiger, where courtesy and careful conduct keep you safe
hexagrams.now: The image is stepping on the tail of a tiger without being bitten. You may be dealing with a powerful person, a sensitive situation or a risky step. The traditional text says this can succeed — through careful, courteous and sincere conduct. Know your place and the power of those around you, but do not be paralysed by fear. Good manners, clear boundaries and inner calm let you move through danger safely.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a delicate phase. Courtesy, respect for others and careful conduct will be essential.
do: Know clearly what you value and what your boundaries are
Move carefully when others hold power
avoid: Provoking someone who is more powerful
hexagrams.love: Be respectful and considerate. Small gestures of courtesy prevent unnecessary hurt.
hexagrams.work: Handle powerful people diplomatically. Know the rules and follow them while pursuing your goals.
hexagrams.self: Pay attention to how you conduct yourself, not just what you want. Your manner shapes the outcome.
hexagrams.jung: Treading the tiger's tail may mirror our relationship with powerful instinctive forces. They cannot be denied, but they can be approached with respect and awareness rather than recklessness.
hexagrams.example: Negotiating with a demanding boss, approaching a difficult conversation with a family member, or entering an unfamiliar culture.
hexagrams.judgment: (Lî suggests the idea of) one treading on the tail of a tiger, which does not bite him. There will be progress and success.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the sky above, and below it (that representing the waters of) a marsh, form Lî. The superior man, in accordance with this, discriminates between high and low, and gives settlement to the aims of the people.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject treading his accustomed path. If he go forward, there will be no error.
lines.plain: Simple conduct. Moving forward plainly and honestly, without ambition, brings no blame.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject treading the path that is level and easy;--a quiet and solitary man, to whom, if he be firm and correct, there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Treading a smooth, level path. The quiet, unassuming person who keeps to the middle way has good fortune.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows a one-eyed man (who thinks he) can see; a lame man (who thinks he) can walk well; one who treads on the tail of a tiger and is bitten. (All this indicates) ill fortune. We have a (mere) bravo acting the part of a great ruler.
lines.plain: A one-eyed person who thinks they can see, a lame person who thinks they can walk: they step on the tiger's tail and are bitten. Overestimating yourself brings misfortune.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject treading on the tail of a tiger. He becomes full of apprehensive caution, and in the end there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Stepping on the tiger's tail with great caution. Careful, attentive conduct brings good fortune in the end.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the resolute tread of its subject. Though he be firm and correct, there will be peril.
lines.plain: Resolute conduct. Being determined is necessary, but be aware of the danger it brings.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, tells us to look at (the whole course) that is trodden, and examine the presage which that gives. If it be complete and without failure, there will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: Look back at how you have conducted yourself and examine the signs. If your conduct has been complete and sincere, great good fortune follows.

hexagrams.name: Peace
hexagrams.core: a time of peace and harmony, when communication flows and things can flourish
hexagrams.now: Heaven and earth unite, and all things flourish. Peace describes a period in which forces that are often opposed — high and low, strong and gentle — are in communication. Relationships improve, work moves forward and the small departs while the great arrives. It is a time of good fortune, but the text also hints that peace must be cared for: harmony is a living balance, not a permanent possession. Enjoy it, share it and use it to strengthen foundations.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward greater harmony and cooperation, a time when things can flourish if you keep communication open.
do: Strengthen relationships while things are good
Use calm times to build lasting foundations
avoid: Assuming harmony will last without care
hexagrams.love: A good time for closeness, understanding and mutual support. Nurture it with honest communication.
hexagrams.work: Cooperation and teamwork thrive. Expand carefully and build on shared success.
hexagrams.self: Enjoy a sense of balance. Use it to establish habits that will support you in harder times.
hexagrams.jung: Peace may symbolize a state in which conscious and unconscious are in communication rather than conflict. The upper and lower parts of the psyche meet and exchange energy, often experienced as wellbeing and creativity.
hexagrams.example: A family reconciling after tension, a team that finally works well together, or a period of stability after a difficult year.
hexagrams.judgment: In Thâi (we see) the little gone and the great come. (It indicates that) there will be good fortune, with progress and success.
hexagrams.image: (The trigrams for) heaven and earth in communication together form Thâi. The (sage) sovereign, in harmony with this, fashions and completes (his regulations) after the courses of heaven and earth, and assists the application of the adaptations furnished by them,--in order to benefit the people.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of grass pulled up, and bringing with it other stalks with whose roots it is connected. Advance (on the part of its subject) will be fortunate.
lines.plain: Pull up one blade of grass and others come with it. Moving forward together with like-minded people brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows one who can bear with the uncultivated, will cross the Ho without a boat, does not forget the distant, and has no (selfish) friendships. Thus does he prove himself acting in accordance with the course of the due Mean.
lines.plain: Bear with the uncultured, cross the river resolutely, do not neglect what is distant and do not form cliques. Broad-minded tolerance keeps to the middle way.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows that, while there is no state of peace that is not liable to be disturbed, and no departure (of evil men) so that they shall not return, yet when one is firm and correct, as he realises the distresses that may arise, he will commit no error. There is no occasion for sadness at the certainty (of such recurring changes); and in this mood the happiness (of the present) may be (long) enjoyed.
lines.plain: There is no plain without a slope, no going without a return. Change is inevitable. Stay firm and sincere in hard times, and you will still enjoy your good fortune.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject fluttering (down);--not relying on his own rich resources, but calling in his neighbours. (They all come) not as having received warning, but in the sincerity (of their hearts).
lines.plain: Fluttering down, not relying on wealth, joining with neighbours sincerely. People unite because they share real trust.

lines.legge: The fifth six, divided, reminds us of (king) Tî-yî's (rule about the) marriage of his younger sister. By such a course there is happiness and there will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: The emperor gives his younger sister in marriage. Humble, generous union brings blessings and great good fortune.

lines.legge: The sixth six, divided, shows us the city wall returned into the moat. It is not the time to use the army. (The subject of the line) may, indeed, announce his orders to the people of his own city; but however correct and firm he may be, he will have cause for regret.
lines.plain: The city wall crumbles back into the moat. Peace is ending; do not use force. Accept the change and attend to your own circle.

hexagrams.name: Standstill
hexagrams.core: a period of standstill, when communication breaks down and integrity matters more than advancement
hexagrams.now: Heaven and earth no longer communicate. Standstill describes a time when things do not move: people misunderstand each other, efforts produce little and the wrong influences may be gaining ground. The text advises the superior person to hold back, keep to their values and not be tempted by rewards from unworthy sources. This is not a permanent condition. Standstill always ends, and those who keep their integrity will be ready when things move again.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a period of standstill, when patience and integrity matter more than pushing forward.
do: Prepare quietly for when things change
avoid: Compromising your principles for short-term gain
Forcing communication that is not being received
hexagrams.love: If communication has broken down, do not push. Take time to understand what is blocking connection.
hexagrams.work: Progress may stall. Use this time to reassess, protect your reputation and avoid questionable deals.
hexagrams.self: You may feel stuck. Hold to what you know is right and trust that stagnation passes.
hexagrams.jung: Standstill can describe a psychological state in which the flow between conscious and unconscious is blocked: life feels flat and meaningless. Such periods can be a necessary pause before renewal.
hexagrams.example: A workplace where management and staff no longer listen to each other, or a relationship stuck in the same argument.
hexagrams.judgment: In Phî there is the want of good understanding between the (different classes of) men, and its indication is unfavourable to the firm and correct course of the superior man. We see in it the great gone and the little come.
hexagrams.image: (The trigrams of) heaven and earth, not in intercommunication, form Phî. The superior man, in accordance with this, restrains (the manifestation) of) his virtue, and avoids the calamities (that threaten him). There is no opportunity of conferring on him the glory of emolument.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, suggests the idea of grass pulled up, and bringing with it other stalks with whose roots it is connected. With firm correctness (on the part of its subject), there will be good fortune and progress.
lines.plain: Pull up one blade of grass and others come with it. Withdraw together with like-minded people. Staying firm brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject patient and obedient. To the small man (comporting himself so) there will be good fortune. If the great man (comport himself) as the distress and obstruction require, he will have success.
lines.plain: Patience and compliance help ordinary people, but the great person accepts standstill and does not compromise. This leads to success.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject ashamed of the purpose folded (in his breast).
lines.plain: Hidden shame. Recognizing what you have done wrong is the first step to change.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject acting in accordance with the ordination (of Heaven), and committing no error. His companions will come and share in his happiness.
lines.plain: Acting according to a higher calling, without blame. Those who share the same values will find blessings.

lines.legge: In the fifth NINE, undivided, we see him who brings the distress and obstruction to a close,--the great man and fortunate. (But let him say), 'We may perish! We may perish!' (so shall the state of things become firm, as if) bound to a clump of bushy mulberry trees.
lines.plain: Standstill is ending. Remain alert: "What if it should fail? What if it should fail?" Care makes success secure, like tying it to a mulberry tree.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the overthrow (and removal of) the condition of distress and obstruction. Before this there was that condition. Hereafter there will be joy.
lines.plain: Standstill is overturned. First there is obstruction, then there is joy.

hexagrams.name: Fellowship
hexagrams.core: a time of fellowship, when open cooperation around shared values achieves what individuals cannot
hexagrams.now: Fellowship describes people united by a shared purpose, like fire rising toward heaven. True community is built on openness and common values, not on private interests or narrow cliques. The text says fellowship "in the open" brings success and makes it possible to cross the great water — to achieve great things together. Look for where you can cooperate, include others and build trust across differences.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward cooperation and community. Shared goals and open-mindedness will make progress possible.
do: Look for common ground with others
hexagrams.love: Shared values and friendship are the foundation now. Do things together that matter to both of you.
hexagrams.work: Collaborate openly. Build alliances across teams or departments.
hexagrams.self: Connect with communities that share your values. You do not have to do everything alone.
hexagrams.jung: Fellowship can symbolize the integration of different parts of the personality around a common purpose. Outwardly, it reflects the human need for community. Inwardly, it suggests reconciling conflicting aspects of yourself.
hexagrams.example: Volunteers organizing a neighbourhood event, a team working on a shared project, or friends supporting each other through change.
hexagrams.judgment: Thung Zăn (or 'Union of men') appears here (as we find it) in the (remote districts of the) country, indicating progress and success. It will be advantageous to cross the great stream. It will be advantageous to maintain the firm correctness of the superior man.
hexagrams.image: (The trigrams for) heaven and fire form Thung Zăn. The superior man, in accordance with this), distinguishes things according to their kinds and classes.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, (shows the representative of) the union of men just issuing from his gate. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Fellowship at the gate. Open cooperation from the start brings no blame.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, (shows the representative of) the union of men in relation with his kindred. There will be occasion for regret.
lines.plain: Fellowship limited to your own clan. Narrow loyalties lead to regret.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) with his arms hidden in the thick grass, and at the top of a high mound. (But) for three years he makes no demonstration.
lines.plain: Weapons hidden in the bushes; watching from a high hill. Suspicion prevents fellowship for a long time.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) mounted on the city wall; but he does not proceed to make the attack (he contemplates). There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Climbing the wall but not attacking. Realizing you cannot win by force, you turn back — good fortune.

lines.legge: In the fifth NINE, undivided, (the representative of) the union of men first wails and cries out, and then laughs. His great host conquers, and he (and the subject of the second line) meet together.
lines.plain: Friends first weep and then laugh. After struggle, great forces come together and meet.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, (shows the representative of) the union of men in the suburbs. There will be no occasion for repentance.
lines.plain: Fellowship in the meadow outside the city. Not the deepest union, but no regret.

hexagrams.name: Possession in Great Measure
hexagrams.core: a time of abundance and success, which lasts when it is handled with modesty, clarity and generosity
hexagrams.now: Fire high in the heavens shines on everything below. This hexagram describes great possession: success, resources or influence. The text promises supreme success. The real question is how you use what you have. Abundance brings responsibility. Modesty, generosity and good judgment keep success healthy, while pride and wastefulness undermine it. Make sure your success serves something good.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward success and abundance. It will be important to use your resources wisely and generously.
do: Support good causes and good people
hexagrams.love: Share your good fortune and appreciation generously. Do not let success create distance.
hexagrams.work: A prosperous time. Invest wisely, reward your team and avoid overconfidence.
hexagrams.self: Recognize your blessings and consider how to share them.
hexagrams.jung: Great Possession may point to psychic wealth: talents, energy and insight. The task is to use them consciously, without becoming inflated by them.
hexagrams.example: Receiving a promotion, an inheritance or recognition, and deciding how to use it responsibly.
hexagrams.judgment: Tâ Yû indicates that, (under the circumstances which it implies), there will be great progress and success.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram for) heaven and (that of) fire above it form Tâ Yû The superior man, in accordance with this, represses what is evil and gives distinction to what is good, in sympathy with the excellent Heaven-conferred (nature).

lines.legge: In the first NINE, undivided, there is no approach to what is injurious, and there is no error. Let there be a realisation of the difficulty (and danger of the position), and there will be no error (to the end).
lines.plain: No relationship with harm yet. Abundance has not caused problems; stay aware of difficulty and remain blameless.

lines.legge: In the second NINE, undivided, we have a large waggon with its load. In whatever direction advance is made, there will be no error.
lines.plain: A big wagon for loading. You have the means to carry a great deal. Move forward; there is no blame.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows us a feudal prince presenting his offerings to the Son of Heaven. A small man would be unequal (to such a duty).
lines.plain: A prince offers his wealth to the Son of Heaven. Use your resources for a higher purpose; a petty person cannot do this.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject keeping his great resources under restraint. There will be no error.
lines.plain: He does not show off his wealth. Restraint and modesty keep you free from blame.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows the sincerity of its subject reciprocated by that of all the others (represented in the hexagram). Let him display a proper majesty, and there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Sincerity that is accessible yet dignified. Natural authority brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject with help accorded to him from Heaven. There will be good fortune, advantage in every respect.
lines.plain: Blessed by heaven. Good fortune; nothing that does not benefit.

hexagrams.name: Modesty
hexagrams.core: a time when modesty and quiet strength bring success, balancing too much and too little
hexagrams.now: A mountain hidden within the earth: great strength that does not display itself. Modesty describes a person who has real worth but does not boast. The text says modesty brings success and allows the superior person to carry things through to completion. Modesty here is not low self-esteem; it is a balanced attitude that reduces excess and increases what is lacking. It creates trust and lasting influence.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase where modesty and quiet competence achieve more than self-promotion.
do: Let your work speak for itself
avoid: False humility used to seek praise
hexagrams.love: Show appreciation and avoid trying to look superior. Humility creates closeness.
hexagrams.work: Quiet competence will be noticed. Credit others generously.
hexagrams.self: Measure yourself honestly — not too high, not too low.
hexagrams.jung: Modesty may describe an ego that does not inflate itself, either upward into grandiosity or downward into worthlessness. It is in right relationship to the larger Self.
hexagrams.example: An expert who listens carefully to beginners, or a team leader who shares credit.
hexagrams.judgment: Khien indicates progress and success. The superior man, (being humble as it implies), will have a (good) issue (to his undertakings).
hexagrams.image: (The trigram for) the earth and (that of) a mountain in the midst of it form Khien. The superior man, in accordance with this, diminishes what is excessive (in himself), and increases where there is any defect, bringing about an equality, according to the nature of the case, in his treatment (of himself and others).

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows us the superior man who adds humility to humility. (Even) the great stream may be crossed with this, and there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Very modest. The superior person crosses great water. Humility makes big undertakings possible.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows us humility that has made itself recognised. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Modesty that comes to expression. Recognized humility brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows the superior man of (acknowledged) merit. He will maintain his success to the end, and have good fortune.
lines.plain: Hard-working modesty. Labour without boasting brings success to completion.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one, whose action would be in every way advantageous, stirring up (the more) his humility.
lines.plain: Nothing that does not benefit modesty in action. Use humility actively, not as passivity.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows one who, without being rich, is able to employ his neighbours. He may advantageously use the force of arms. All his movements will be advantageous.
lines.plain: Without relying on wealth, you win the support of your neighbours. Firm, even forceful, action is justified now when something must be corrected.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided, shows us humility that has made itself recognised. The subject of it will with advantage put his hosts in motion; but (he will only) punish his own towns and state.
lines.plain: Modesty that has been recognized. Using it, you can set things right in your own sphere.

hexagrams.name: Enthusiasm
hexagrams.core: a time of enthusiasm and inspired energy, which moves people when it is grounded and sincere
hexagrams.now: Thunder bursts from the earth: energy is released and people are stirred. Enthusiasm describes a time of inspiration, motivation and shared feeling. The text says it is good for setting up helpers and putting armies in motion — mobilizing people. Enthusiasm is powerful but needs grounding. Joy that comes from genuine harmony moves people; excitement that is self-indulgent or empty fades quickly. Be sincere, prepared and attentive to the mood of others.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase of enthusiasm and mobilization. Inspired energy can move people if it is sincere and well-directed.
do: Prepare and organize so energy is not wasted
hexagrams.love: Bring joy and playfulness into the relationship, but stay attentive to how the other person really feels.
hexagrams.work: A good time to inspire a team or launch a campaign. Plan carefully so energy translates into results.
hexagrams.self: Follow what genuinely excites you, but do not lose yourself in pleasure.
hexagrams.jung: Enthusiasm can describe a surge of psychic energy, often from the unconscious. Such energy can heal and inspire, but can also overwhelm judgement if it is not integrated.
hexagrams.example: Starting a new hobby with excitement, motivating a team before a big event, or the joy of a celebration.
hexagrams.judgment: Yü indicates that, (in the state which it implies), feudal princes may be set up, and the hosts put in motion, with advantage.
hexagrams.image: (The trigrams for) the earth and thunder issuing from it with its crashing noise form Yü. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, composed their music and did honour to virtue, presenting it especially and most grandly to God, when they associated with Him (at the service) their highest ancestor and their father.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject proclaiming his pleasure and satisfaction. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Boasting about one's enthusiasm. Self-indulgent display brings misfortune.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows one who is firm as a rock. (He sees a thing) without waiting till it has come to pass; with his firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Firm as a rock. Recognizing the signs early and acting correctly brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows one looking up (for favours), while he indulges the feeling of pleasure and satisfaction. If he would understand!--If he be late in doing so, there will indeed be occasion for repentance.
lines.plain: Looking upward for enthusiasm, waiting for approval. Hesitation brings regret.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows him from whom the harmony and satisfaction come. Great is the success which he obtains. Let him not allow suspicions to enter his mind, and thus friends will gather around him.
lines.plain: The source of enthusiasm. Great achievements are possible; do not doubt and others will gather around you.

lines.legge: The fifth six, divided, shows one with a chronic complaint, but who lives on without dying.
lines.plain: Chronically ill but not dying. Persistent pressure keeps you from false enthusiasm and helps you survive.

lines.legge: The topmost six, divided, shows its subject with darkened mind devoted to the pleasure and satisfaction (of the time); but if he change his course even when (it may be considered as) completed, there will be no error.
lines.plain: Deluded enthusiasm. If you change course even late, there is no blame.

hexagrams.name: Following
hexagrams.core: a time to follow wisely, adapting to circumstances and to worthy leadership without losing your principles
hexagrams.now: Thunder rests within the lake: energy adapts to the season. Following describes a time when the right response is to adapt and follow — whether that means following a worthy leader, a natural rhythm or the needs of the moment. The text promises supreme success when following remains correct. Good following is not blind obedience; it is choosing what deserves to be followed. Equally, if you lead, people will follow you willingly only if you first serve their needs.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase of adaptation, when flexibility and wise choices about whom or what to follow are important.
do: Choose carefully what and whom you follow
Rest and recover when the time calls for it
avoid: Following blindly or for selfish gain
hexagrams.love: Be willing to adapt to your partner's needs and rhythms, while staying true to yourself.
hexagrams.work: Follow good leadership or adapt to market conditions. Leading by serving others earns loyalty.
hexagrams.self: Let go of rigidity. Flexibility can be a sign of strength.
hexagrams.jung: Following may describe the ego's willingness to follow the guidance of the deeper Self, which Jung saw as the center and guide of psychological development. It also raises the question of projection: whom do we follow, and why?
hexagrams.example: Joining a respected mentor's project, adapting to a new workplace culture, or responding to a child's changing needs.
hexagrams.judgment: Sui indicates that (under its conditions) there will be great progress and success. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. There will (then) be no error.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram for the waters of) a marsh and (that for) thunder (hidden) in the midst of it form Sui. The superior man in accordance with this, when it is getting towards dark, enters (his house) and rests.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows us one changing the object of his pursuit; but if he be firm and correct, there will he good fortune. Going beyond (his own) gate to find associates, he will achieve merit.
lines.plain: The standard changes. Go out of your own door to mix with others; achievements come.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows us one who cleaves to the little boy, and lets go the man of age and experience.
lines.plain: Clinging to the little boy, you lose the strong man. Do not attach yourself to the wrong person or the lesser option.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows us one who cleaves to the man of age and experience, and lets go. the little boy. Such following will get what it seeks; but it will be advantageous to adhere to what is firm and correct.
lines.plain: Clinging to the strong man, you let go of the little boy. Following what is worthy means giving something up. Stay firm.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows us one followed and obtaining (adherents). Though he be firm and correct, there will be evil. If he be sincere (however) in his course, and make that evident, into what error will he fall?
lines.plain: Following brings success, but persistence in this brings misfortune if motives are selfish. Sincerity and clarity remove blame.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows us (the ruler) sincere in (fostering all) that is excellent. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Sincere in pursuing the good. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows us (that sincerity) firmly held and clung to, yea, and bound fast. (We see) the king with it presenting his offerings on the western mountain.
lines.plain: Firmly bound in loyalty. The king offers to the western mountain. Deep commitment that endures.

hexagrams.name: Work on What Has Been Spoiled
hexagrams.core: a time to repair what has decayed, especially problems inherited from the past
hexagrams.now: Wind blows low beneath the mountain, and things become stagnant. The character for this hexagram shows worms in a bowl: something has decayed through neglect. The text says this can lead to great success and advises reflecting on what came three days before and planning what comes three days after — understand the causes, then plan carefully. You may be dealing with problems inherited from the past, perhaps family patterns, old habits or neglected obligations. Repair is possible, but it requires honesty and effort.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time of repair and renewal. Old problems or neglect will need to be faced honestly.
do: Identify the root causes of problems
Plan carefully before and after acting
hexagrams.love: Address old wounds or recurring patterns honestly. Repair trust step by step.
hexagrams.work: Fix underlying problems rather than covering them up. Restructure what is not working.
hexagrams.self: Examine inherited habits and beliefs. Decide which to keep and which to change.
hexagrams.jung: Work on What Has Been Spoiled can point to inherited psychological patterns, family complexes passed from parents to children. Becoming conscious of them is the first step to breaking their hold.
hexagrams.example: Repairing a neglected house, reforming a struggling organization, or healing family relationships after years of tension.
hexagrams.judgment: Kû indicates great progress and success (to him who deals properly with the condition represented by it). There will be advantage in (efforts like that of) crossing the great stream. (He should weigh well, however, the events of) three days before the turning point, and those (to be done) three days after it.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram for) a mountain, and below it that for wind, form Kû. The superior man, in accordance with this, (addresses himself to) help the people and nourish his own virtue.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. If he be an (able) son, the father will escape the blame of having erred. The position is perilous, but there will be good fortune in the end.
lines.plain: Setting right what the father spoiled. If the son is capable, the father is free of blame. Danger exists, but good fortune comes in the end.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his mother. He should not (carry) his firm correctness (to the utmost).
lines.plain: Setting right what the mother spoiled. Be gentle; do not be too rigid.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. There may be some small occasion for repentance, but there will not be any great error.
lines.plain: Setting right what the father spoiled. There may be slight regret, but no great blame.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows (a son) viewing indulgently the troubles caused by his father. If he go forward, he will find cause to regret it.
lines.plain: Tolerating what the father spoiled. Continuing to look away leads to humiliation.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows (a son) dealing with the troubles caused by his father. He obtains the praise of using (the fit instrument for his work).
lines.plain: Setting right what the father spoiled earns praise. Repairing with good help brings honour.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows us one who does not serve either king or feudal lord, but in a lofty spirit prefers (to attend to) his own affairs.
lines.plain: Not serving kings and princes, setting higher goals. Some people step back from public affairs to cultivate inner values.

hexagrams.name: Approach
hexagrams.core: a time of approach and growing influence, when kindness and teaching strengthen relationships before the season turns
hexagrams.now: The earth stands above the lake, close and caring. Approach describes a time when something good draws near: opportunities, influence or relationships grow. The text promises great success but warns that "in the eighth month there will be misfortune" — favourable seasons do not last forever. Use this time well. Approach people with warmth and patience, teach and support others, and prepare for the change that will eventually come.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward growth and new opportunities. Use the favourable time wisely and remember that it will not last forever.
do: Make the most of favourable conditions
Approach people with kindness and patience
avoid: Assuming good times will last forever
hexagrams.love: Draw closer with warmth and care. A good time to deepen connection.
hexagrams.work: Influence is growing. Mentor others and expand thoughtfully.
hexagrams.self: You are growing. Use this momentum to build lasting habits.
hexagrams.jung: Approach may describe the conscious mind drawing near to new content from the unconscious. It is a time of opening and receptivity, when insights and new attitudes can be accepted.
hexagrams.example: A new supervisor getting to know the team, or a growing friendship that is deepening.
hexagrams.judgment: Lin (indicates that under the conditions supposed in it) there will be great progress and success, while it will be advantageous to be firmly correct. In the eighth month there will be evil.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram for) the waters of a marsh and that for the earth above it form Lin. The superior man, in accordance with this, has his purposes of instruction that are inexhaustible, and nourishes and supports the people without limit.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject advancing in company (with the subject of the second line). Through his firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: You draw near together with others who share your aim. Influence that is shared, not grabbed, is welcome now. Stay correct and things go well.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject advancing in company (with the subject of the first line). There will be good fortune; (advancing) will be in every way advantageous.
lines.plain: Drawing near together, with full support. Everything you approach in this spirit is likely to go well, even what is still uncertain.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows one well pleased (indeed) to advance, (but whose action) will be in no way advantageous. If he become anxious about it (however), there will be no error.
lines.plain: Approaching with easy, sweet words but no real substance. Charm without sincerity achieves nothing. If you notice this and become genuinely concerned, the mistake is avoided.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one advancing in the highest mode. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Drawing near fully and wholeheartedly, meeting people where they are. Complete, sincere engagement brings no blame.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows the advance of wisdom, such as befits the great ruler. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Approaching with wisdom, as a good ruler draws on capable people rather than doing everything alone. Delegating wisely brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the advance of honesty and generosity. There will be good fortune, and no error.
lines.plain: Approaching with generosity and depth of heart, even from a position where you could stay aloof. Kindness offered freely brings good fortune and no blame.

hexagrams.name: Contemplation
hexagrams.core: a time of contemplation and observation, when understanding and good example matter more than action
hexagrams.now: Wind moves over the earth, reaching everything. Contemplation shows a tower from which one sees widely, and also a person who is seen by others. The text describes the moment of a ritual when the worshipper has washed their hands but not yet made the offering: full of sincere attention.
