This is a time to observe, reflect and understand before acting. Your example and attitude influence others more than your words.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase of reflection and observation. Understanding the larger picture will be more important than immediate action.
do: Reflect on your own conduct and its effects
hexagrams.love: Observe and understand each other's needs. Quiet attention can deepen intimacy.
hexagrams.work: Step back to see the big picture. Leaders influence by example.
hexagrams.self: A good time for meditation, journaling or reflection.
hexagrams.jung: Contemplation suggests turning attention inward to observe the movements of the psyche. Jung's method of active imagination involves this kind of patient, attentive observation of inner images.
hexagrams.example: A manager observing how a team works before making changes, or a person reflecting on their life before a major decision.
hexagrams.judgment: Kwân shows (how he whom it represents should be like) the worshipper who has washed his hands, but not (yet) presented his offerings;--with sincerity and an appearance of dignity (commanding reverent regard).
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the earth, and that for wind moving above it, form Kwan. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, examined the (different) regions (of the kingdom), to see the (ways of the) people, and set forth their instructions.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows the looking of a lad;--not blamable in men of inferior rank, but matter for regret in superior men.
lines.plain: Boyish contemplation. Shallow viewing is acceptable for ordinary people, but not for those who should know better.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows one peeping out from a door. It would be advantageous if it were (merely) the firm correctness of a female.
lines.plain: Contemplation through a crack in the door. A narrow view; acceptable only in limited contexts.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows one looking at (the course of) his own life, to advance or recede (accordingly).
lines.plain: Contemplating your own life to decide whether to advance or retreat. Self-examination guides your next step.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one contemplating the glory of the kingdom. It will be advantageous for him, being such as he is, (to seek) to be a guest of the king.
lines.plain: Contemplating the light of the kingdom. Learning from those who govern well; be a guest of the king.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject contemplating his own life(-course). A superior man, he will (thus) fall into no error.
lines.plain: Contemplating your own life by looking at its effects on others. If those effects are good, you are on the right path and there is no blame.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject contemplating his character to see if it be indeed that of a superior man. He will not fall into error.
lines.plain: Contemplating your own character, as if from the outside, to see whether it is truly noble. Honest self-examination, even when you are no longer at the center of things, keeps you from error.

hexagrams.name: Biting Through
hexagrams.core: a time to bite through obstacles decisively and fairly, bringing clarity and justice to a stuck situation
hexagrams.now: Thunder and lightning: clarity combined with force. The image shows a mouth with something stuck between the teeth. Biting Through says an obstacle prevents things from coming together, and it must be dealt with energetically. The text favours "the use of legal constraints" — firm but just action. Whatever the obstacle is — a lie, a problem, a blocking person — it must be faced, understood and removed fairly.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a moment that requires decisive action. Obstacles will need to be faced clearly and justly.
hexagrams.love: If something is blocking closeness, address it directly and honestly.
hexagrams.work: Remove the bottleneck. Enforce rules fairly and clarify misunderstandings.
hexagrams.self: Face the habit or belief that keeps getting in the way.
hexagrams.jung: Biting Through may describe the need to confront something unpleasant that the ego would rather avoid — a shadow quality or an uncomfortable truth.
hexagrams.example: Ending a toxic agreement, resolving a long-standing misunderstanding, or confronting dishonest behaviour.
hexagrams.judgment: Shih Ho indicates successful progress (in the condition of things which it supposes). It will be advantageous to use legal constraints.
hexagrams.image: (The trigrams representing) thunder and lightning form Shih Ho. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, framed their penalties with intelligence, and promulgated their laws.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows one with his feet in the stocks and deprived of his toes. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Feet fastened in the stocks, toes hidden. A small punishment early prevents larger mistakes. No blame.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows one biting through the soft flesh, and (going on to) bite off the nose. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Biting through soft meat until the nose disappears. Reacting a little too strongly, but no blame.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows one gnawing dried flesh, and meeting with what is disagreeable. There will be occasion for some small regret, but no (great) error.
lines.plain: Biting through old dried meat and meeting poison. A small humiliation, but no blame.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows one gnawing the flesh dried on the bone, and getting the pledges of money and arrows. It will be advantageous to him to realise the difficulty of his task and be firm,--in which case there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Biting through dried gristly meat and receiving metal arrows. Persist through difficulty. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows one gnawing at dried flesh, and finding the yellow gold. Let him be firm and correct, realising the peril (of his position). There will be no error.
lines.plain: Biting through dried lean meat and receiving yellow gold. Be firm and aware of danger. No blame.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows one wearing the cangue, and deprived of his cars. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Wearing a cangue that covers the ears. Refusing to listen leads to misfortune.

hexagrams.name: Grace
hexagrams.core: a time when beauty and form matter, though grace must remain true to the substance underneath
hexagrams.now: Fire beneath the mountain lights up its beauty. Grace is about appearance, style and culture: the forms that make life pleasant and meaningful. The text says grace brings success in small matters. Beauty is valuable, but it is not enough for important decisions. Make sure the presentation is true to the substance. Elegance is at its best when simple.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase where presentation, beauty and form become important. Keep substance and appearance in harmony.
hexagrams.love: Small gestures of beauty and care can delight, but deep connection needs more than appearance.
hexagrams.work: Present your work well, but do not let polish replace quality.
hexagrams.self: Express yourself creatively. Seek simple, authentic beauty.
hexagrams.jung: Grace may symbolize the persona, the social face we present to the world. Jung saw it as necessary but warned against identifying with it. The question is whether the outer form expresses the inner truth.
hexagrams.example: Preparing a presentation, decorating a home, or choosing an outfit for an important occasion.
hexagrams.judgment: Pî indicates that there should be free course (in what it denotes). There will be little advantage (however) if it be allowed to advance (and take the lead).
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain and that for fire under it form Pî. The superior man, in accordance with this, throws a brilliancy around his various processes of government, but does not dare (in a similar way) to decide cases of criminal litigation.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows one adorning (the way of) his feet. He can discard a carriage and walk on foot.
lines.plain: Gracing the toes, leaving the carriage and walking. Simplicity is better than a borrowed show.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows one adorning his beard.
lines.plain: Gracing the beard. Form follows substance; adornment depends on what it adorns.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject with the appearance of being adorned and bedewed (with rich favours). But let him ever maintain his firm correctness, and there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Graceful and moist. Lasting firmness brings good fortune; do not get lost in comfort.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one looking as if adorned, but only in white. As if (mounted on) a white horse, and furnished with wings, (he seeks union with the subject of the first line), while (the intervening third pursues), not as a robber, but intent on a matrimonial alliance.
lines.plain: Grace or simplicity? A white horse comes as if on wings. A sincere partner, not an enemy, approaches.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject adorned by (the occupants of) the heights and gardens. He bears his roll of silk, small and slight. He may appear stingy; but there will be good fortune in the end.
lines.plain: Grace in the hills and gardens. A small, modest gift. Humiliation at first, then good fortune.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows one with white as his (only) ornament. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Simple grace. Natural simplicity brings no blame.

hexagrams.name: Splitting Apart
hexagrams.core: a time of decline and stripping away, when it is wiser to wait than to push against collapse
hexagrams.now: A mountain rests on the earth, but its base is crumbling. Splitting Apart describes a time when structures are breaking down, often from below. The text says it does not further you to go anywhere. This is not the time for bold action. Protect what is essential, be generous to those who depend on you, and wait. Decay is part of the natural cycle; after it, renewal comes.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase of decline or loss. Protect what is essential and wait for renewal.
do: Protect your core values and resources
Be generous to those who rely on you
hexagrams.love: If a relationship is weakening, focus on what can be preserved rather than blaming. Some things need time.
hexagrams.work: Avoid expansion. Protect essential resources and reputation.
hexagrams.self: Let go of what no longer serves you. Endings make room for beginnings.
hexagrams.jung: Splitting Apart can describe the breakdown of an old attitude or self-image. Painful as it is, such dissolution is often necessary before a new orientation can emerge from the unconscious.
hexagrams.example: A business in decline, the end of a long relationship, or a period of declining health that calls for rest and acceptance.
hexagrams.judgment: Po indicates that (in the state which it symbolises) it will not be advantageous to make a movement in any direction whatever.
hexagrams.image: (The trigrams representing) the earth, and (above it) that for a mountain, which adheres to the earth, form Po. Superiors, in accordance with this, seek to strengthen those below them, to secure the peace and stability of their own position.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows one overturning the couch by injuring its legs. (The injury will go on to) the destruction of (all) firm correctness, and there will be evil.
lines.plain: The bed is being split at its legs. Decay starts at the foundation and undermines those who are loyal and upright. Recognize the danger early; it is serious.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows one overthrowing the couch by injuring its frame. (The injury will go on to) the destruction of (all) firm correctness, and there will be evil.
lines.plain: The damage reaches the frame of the bed. The erosion is spreading closer. Without support, standing firm alone is risky; protect yourself.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject among the overthrowers; but there will be no error.
lines.plain: Among those who are splitting things apart, one stays connected to what is good. Breaking ranks with harmful company is right and brings no blame.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject having overthrown the couch, and (going to injure) the skin (of him who lies on it). There will be evil.
lines.plain: The damage has reached the skin of the person lying on the bed. The danger is no longer distant; it touches you directly. This is a time for great care.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows (its subject leading on the others like) a string of fishes, and (obtaining for them) the favour that lights on the inmates of the palace. There will be advantage in every way.
lines.plain: Like a string of fish led in order, the people are brought into favour. The disorder is steered into a healthy direction, and everything benefits.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as) a great fruit which has not been eaten. The superior man finds (the people again) as a chariot carrying him. The small men (by their course) overthrow their own dwellings.
lines.plain: A large fruit still hangs on the tree, uneaten. A seed of goodness survives the collapse. A person of integrity will be carried by others; a petty person brings ruin on their own house.

hexagrams.name: Return
hexagrams.core: a turning point, when the light returns and something healthy begins again quietly
hexagrams.now: Thunder within the earth: after the darkest point, the light returns. Return marks a turning point. One single solid line enters at the bottom, beneath five broken lines. The text says going out and coming in are without error, friends come, and on the seventh day comes return. Renewal begins quietly. Do not rush it. Rest, recover and let the new energy grow naturally. Returning to what is healthy, true and natural brings success.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a turning point and a fresh start. Let new energy grow gently, without forcing it.
do: Return to healthy habits and true values
hexagrams.love: A chance to reconnect or reconcile. Begin gently and rebuild trust.
hexagrams.work: A good moment to restart a project or return to core strengths.
hexagrams.self: Return to what nourishes you: rest, nature, honest reflection.
hexagrams.jung: Return may describe the moment when psychic energy, after a period of depression or withdrawal, begins to flow back into consciousness. Jung called the return of libido after introversion a renewal of life.
hexagrams.example: Recovering after an illness, returning to an old passion, or reconciling after a falling-out.
hexagrams.judgment: Fû indicates that there will be free course and progress (in what it denotes). (The subject of it) finds no one to distress him in his exits and entrances; friends come to him, and no error is committed. He will return and repeat his (proper) course. In seven days comes his return. There will be advantage in whatever direction movement is made.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for thunder in the midst of it form Fû. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, on the day. of the (winter) solstice, shut the gates of the passes (from one state to another), so that the travelling merchants could not (then) pursue their journeys, nor the princes go on with the inspection of their states.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject returning (from an error) of no great extent, which would not proceed to anything requiring repentance. There will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: Turning back after only a short distance on the wrong path. Correcting a mistake early means there is nothing to regret. Great good fortune.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows the admirable return (of its subject). There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: A gentle, admirable return, helped by the good example of others. Coming back to what is right without stubbornness brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows one who has made repeated returns. The position is perilous, but there will be no error.
lines.plain: Returning again and again after repeated lapses. It is risky to keep slipping, but every return is still the right choice, so there is no blame.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject moving right in the centre (among those represented by the other divided lines), and yet returning alone (to his proper path).
lines.plain: Walking in the middle of a crowd, you alone turn back to what is right. Following your conscience rather than the group is the right path.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows the noble return of its subject. There will be no ground for repentance.
lines.plain: A generous, sincere return of the heart. When the return comes from honest self-examination, there is no regret.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject all astray on the subject of returning. There will be evil. There will be calamities and errors. If with his views he put the hosts in motion, the end will be a great defeat, whose issues will extend to the ruler of the state. Even in ten years he will not be able to repair the disaster.
lines.plain: Missing the moment to return and staying on the wrong course. This leads to misfortune that lasts. Forcing things through, especially with aggression, makes it worse for years.

hexagrams.name: Innocence
hexagrams.core: a time to act with sincerity and innocence, free of hidden motives, while accepting the unexpected
hexagrams.now: Thunder rolls under heaven, and all things are set in their true nature. Innocence describes acting naturally and sincerely, without calculation or hidden motives. The text promises supreme success to those who stay correct, but warns that anyone who is not as they should be will meet misfortune. Unexpected events may happen — some good, some not. The best response is to remain genuine, not to scheme. Act because it is right, not because of what you hope to gain.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time when sincerity and spontaneity matter, and unexpected events test whether your motives are clear.
do: Do the right thing without calculating rewards
avoid: Rash actions based on wishful thinking
hexagrams.love: Be genuine and spontaneous; do not play games. Honest feeling is your strength.
hexagrams.work: Do good work for its own sake. Avoid schemes or shortcuts.
hexagrams.self: Reconnect with your natural, unguarded self.
hexagrams.jung: Innocence may suggest acting from the Self rather than the calculating ego. It can also point to the role of chance and the unexpected, the area where Jung located synchronicity.
hexagrams.example: Helping someone without expecting thanks, or responding honestly to an unexpected turn of events.
hexagrams.judgment: Wû Wang indicates great progress and success, while there will be advantage in being firm and correct. If (its subject and his action) be not correct, he will fall into errors, and it will not be advantageous for him to move in any direction.
hexagrams.image: The thunder rolls all under the sky, and to (every)thing there is given (its nature), free from all insincerity. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, (made their regulations) in complete accordance with the seasons, thereby nourishing all things.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject free from all insincerity. His advance will be accompanied with good fortune.
lines.plain: Acting from innocence, with no hidden motive. When your intentions are simple and sincere, moving forward brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows one who reaps without having ploughed (that he might reap), and gathers the produce of his third year's fields without having cultivated them the first year for that end. To such a one there will be advantage in whatever direction he may move.
lines.plain: Ploughing without counting on the harvest, clearing land without calculating its future value. Do the work for its own sake rather than for the reward, and progress follows.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows calamity happening to one who is free from insincerity;--as in the case of an ox that has been tied up. A passer by finds it (and carries it off), while the people in the neighbourhood have the calamity (of being accused and. apprehended).
lines.plain: Undeserved misfortune: a passer-by takes the tethered ox, and the villagers are blamed. Sometimes trouble falls on you without any fault of yours. Keep your integrity and do not take it personally.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows (a case) in which, if its subject can remain firm and correct, there will be no error.
lines.plain: Remain firm and true to yourself. If you can keep to what is right, no mistake will be made.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows one who is free from insincerity, and yet has fallen ill. Let him not use medicine, and he will have occasion for joy (in his recovery).
lines.plain: An illness you did not cause. Do not rush to medicine or drastic remedies; this kind of trouble often clears up by itself. Avoid overreacting.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject free from insincerity, yet sure to fall into error, if he take action. (His action) will not be advantageous in any way.
lines.plain: Acting now, even with innocent motives, will go wrong. The timing is not right. Wait rather than moving forward.

hexagrams.name: The Taming Power of the Great
hexagrams.core: a time of great accumulation, when restraint and learning build strength that will later be released
hexagrams.now: Heaven within the mountain: great creative power is held, stored and nourished. This hexagram describes building up resources, knowledge and character through restraint and daily discipline. The text says it furthers you not to eat at home — that is, to take up public service — and to cross the great water. Hold your strength in check now, so that when you act, you act with great power. Study the words and deeds of the past to build your inner strength.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase of accumulation and discipline, when strength is gathered and held in reserve before being used.
do: Build up knowledge, skill and resources
hexagrams.love: Commitment grows through patience and shared discipline. Build something lasting together.
hexagrams.work: Invest in skills and preparation. A larger opportunity will come.
hexagrams.self: Develop your character and inner strength through daily practice.
hexagrams.jung: Great Accumulation may suggest the containment of libido or psychic energy, holding it rather than discharging it at once, so that it can transform into something new.
hexagrams.example: Training for a long race, studying for a qualification, or saving to start a business.
hexagrams.judgment: Under the conditions of Tâ Khû it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. (If its subject do not seek to) enjoy his revenues in his own family (without taking service at court), there will be good fortune. It will be advantageous for him to cross the great stream.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and in the midst of it that (representing) heaven, form Tâ Khû. The superior man, in accordance with this, stores largely in his memory the words and deeds of former men, to subserve the accumulation of his virtue.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject in a position of peril. It will be advantageous for him to stop his advance.
lines.plain: Danger is ahead. Stopping is wiser than pressing on. Strength that holds itself back now is preserved for later.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows a carriage with the strap under it removed.
lines.plain: The axle strap of the cart has been removed. You are being held back and cannot move, and that is acceptable. Accept the pause without resentment.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject urging his way with good horses. It will be advantageous for him to realise the difficulty (of his course), and to be firm and correct, exercising himself daily in his charioteering and methods of defence; then there will be advantage in whatever direction he may advance.
lines.plain: Good horses race forward, but the path is still hard. Train daily, practise your skills and stay alert; then it is good to have a destination.

lines.legge: The fourth six, divided, shows the young bull, (and yet) having the piece of wood over his horns. There will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: A board fixed to the horns of a young bull. Restraining a force while it is still young and manageable prevents harm later. Great good fortune.

lines.legge: The fifth six, divided, shows the teeth of a castrated hog. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The tusks of a gelded boar. Rather than fighting aggression directly, remove its root. This kind of wise restraint brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as) in command of the firmament of heaven. There will be progress.
lines.plain: The road of heaven lies open. The time of restraint is over; accumulated strength can now move freely toward success.

hexagrams.name: Nourishment
hexagrams.core: a time to examine what nourishes you and others, physically, emotionally and spiritually
hexagrams.now: Thunder beneath the mountain, like the movement of the jaw. Nourishment is about what sustains life — food, words, relationships and ideas. The text advises paying attention to what a person seeks to fill their mouth with: what you nourish, and how you nourish others, reveals your character. Be careful with your words and moderate in consumption. Nourish what is best in yourself and others.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time when nourishment and care become central — what you feed yourself and others in body, mind and spirit.
do: Look at what you consume — food, media, relationships
hexagrams.love: Care for each other's wellbeing. Kind words nourish a relationship.
hexagrams.work: Look after your team's wellbeing. Invest in what truly sustains the organization.
hexagrams.self: Examine your habits: what feeds you and what drains you?
hexagrams.jung: Nourishment may point to the question of what feeds the psyche — which images, relationships and values sustain inner life. It can also suggest the mother archetype: care and dependence.
hexagrams.example: Improving your diet, choosing healthier relationships, or caring for a sick family member.
hexagrams.judgment: Î indicates that with firm correctness there will be good fortune (in what is denoted by it). We must look at what we are seeking to nourish, and by the exercise of our thoughts seek for the proper aliment.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain and under it that for thunder form Î. The superior man, in accordance with this, (enjoins) watchfulness over our words, and the temperate regulation of our eating and drinking.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, (seems to be thus addressed), 'You leave your efficacious tortoise, and look at me till your lower jaw hangs down.' There will be evil.
lines.plain: You let go of your own spiritual resources, your "magic tortoise", and stare enviously at someone else's food. Envy and dependence weaken you. Return to what can nourish you from within.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows one looking downwards for nourishment, which is contrary to what is proper; or seeking it from the height (above), advance towards which will lead to evil.
lines.plain: Seeking nourishment in the wrong way: turning to those beneath you, or reaching for a high hill you have no claim on. Depending on the wrong sources leads to trouble.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows one acting contrary to the method of nourishing. However firm he may be, there will be evil. For ten years let him not take any action, (for) it will not be in any way advantageous.
lines.plain: Turning away from what truly nourishes. Even if this seems justified, it leads to misfortune that can last a long time. Nothing good comes from this approach.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows one looking downwards for (the power to) nourish. There will be good fortune. Looking with a tiger's downward unwavering glare, and with his desire that impels him to spring after spring, he will fall into no error.
lines.plain: Looking upward for help so you can nourish others is right. Like a tiger with a steady gaze, pursue this goal intensely and without selfishness. No blame.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows one acting contrary to what is regular and proper; but if he abide in firmness, there will be good fortune. He should not, (however, try to) cross the great stream.
lines.plain: You are not able to follow the normal path and must depend on others. Staying firm and steady is good, but do not attempt major risks now.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows him from whom comes the nourishing. His position is perilous, but there will be good fortune. It will be advantageous to cross the great stream.
lines.plain: You are the source from which others are nourished. This is a heavy responsibility, so be aware of the danger; carried out conscientiously, it brings good fortune and it is right to undertake great things.

hexagrams.name: Preponderance of the Great
hexagrams.core: a time of extraordinary pressure, like a beam about to give way, that calls for decisive but careful action
hexagrams.now: The lake rises above the trees: too much water. Preponderance of the Great describes a situation in which pressure is too much — the ridgepole of a house is sagging under the weight. The text says it furthers you to have somewhere to go: action is needed. Extraordinary times call for extraordinary measures, but they must be thoughtful and balanced. Do not panic, and do not freeze. Find a way to relieve the pressure.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a critical point where pressure becomes too great and decisive but careful action will be needed.
do: Recognize when pressure is too great
Stay calm and independent in mind
hexagrams.love: The relationship may be under strain. Address the pressure honestly before something breaks.
hexagrams.work: You may be overloaded. Delegate, restructure or seek support.
hexagrams.self: You are carrying too much. Take steps to lighten the load.
hexagrams.jung: Preponderance of the Great can describe a situation where the conscious attitude has become one-sided, and pressure from the unconscious builds until something must give way.
hexagrams.example: Being overwhelmed by work, caring for a sick relative alone, or a business facing a crisis.
hexagrams.judgment: Tâ Kwo suggests to us a beam that is weak. There will be advantage in moving (under its conditions) in any direction whatever; there will be success.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) trees hidden beneath that for the waters of a marsh forms Tâ Kwo. The superior man, in accordance with this, stands up alone and has no fear, and keeps retired from the world without regret.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows one placing mats of the white mâo grass under things set on the ground. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Laying a mat of white rushes beneath something precious. Being extremely careful at the start of an extraordinary undertaking brings no blame.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows a decayed willow producing shoots, or an old husband in possession of his young wife. There will be advantage in every way.
lines.plain: A withered willow puts out new shoots, and an older man marries a young wife. Renewal is possible even late. Unconventional connections can bring fresh life.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows a beam that is weak. There will be evil.
lines.plain: The ridgepole sags dangerously. Pushing ahead on your own strength alone, without help, leads to misfortune.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows a beam curving upwards. There will be good fortune. If (the subject of it) looks for other (help but that of line one), there will be cause for regret.
lines.plain: The ridgepole is braced and holds. Good fortune, provided you do not lean on other, selfish motives. Stay focused on the real task.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows a decayed willow producing flowers, or an old wife in possession of her young husband. There will be occasion neither for blame nor for praise.
lines.plain: A withered willow produces flowers, and an older woman takes a young husband. Something blossoms briefly but bears little fruit. It is not blameworthy, but it is not praiseworthy either.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with extraordinary (boldness) wading through a stream, till the water hides the crown of his head. There will be evil, but no ground for blame.
lines.plain: Wading into deep water until it covers your head. You may be sacrificing yourself for something that needs doing. The outcome is difficult, yet no blame attaches to the motive.

hexagrams.name: The Abysmal
hexagrams.core: a time of repeated danger, which you pass through by staying sincere and moving steadily like flowing water
hexagrams.now: Water upon water: danger repeated. The Abysmal describes a situation in which difficulty follows difficulty. The text says that if you are sincere, you have success in your heart, and whatever you do succeeds. Water teaches how to deal with danger: it flows on, filling every hollow, never losing its nature. Do not panic or freeze. Hold to your sincerity and keep moving steadily, one step at a time.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward repeated difficulties. Steadiness, sincerity and persistence will carry you through.
do: Take one careful step at a time
hexagrams.love: Stay honest and steady through difficulties. Shared hardship can deepen trust.
hexagrams.work: Navigate risk carefully. Keep a steady course and do not cut corners.
hexagrams.self: You may feel caught in recurring struggles. Look for the pattern and keep your inner sincerity.
hexagrams.jung: The Abysmal often symbolizes the unconscious itself, the dark water in which consciousness can drown or from which it can be renewed. It suggests facing fear rather than fleeing it.
hexagrams.example: Going through a series of setbacks, coping with anxiety, or facing a difficult period with patience.
hexagrams.judgment: Khan, here repeated, shows the possession of sincerity, through which the mind is. penetrating. Action (in accordance with this) will be of high value.
hexagrams.image: (The representation of) water flowing on continuously forms the repeated Khan. The superior man, in accordance with this, maintains constantly the virtue (of his heart) and (the integrity of) his conduct, and practises the business of instruction.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject in the double defile, and (yet) entering a cavern within it. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Getting used to danger until you fall into a pit within the pit. Becoming too familiar with risky situations makes you careless and leads to harm.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject in all the peril of the defile. He will, however, get a little (of the deliverance) that he seeks.
lines.plain: You are in danger and cannot escape entirely. Aim only for small gains now. Step by step, you can still make progress.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject, whether he comes or goes ( =descends or ascends), confronted by a defile. All is peril to him and unrest. (His endeavours) will lead him into the cavern of the pit. There should be no action (in such a case).
lines.plain: Danger behind, danger ahead. Any move risks falling deeper. Stop and wait rather than acting rashly.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject (at a feast), with (simply) a bottle of spirits, and a subsidiary basket of rice, while (the cups and bowls) are (only) of earthenware. He introduces his important lessons (as his ruler's) intelligence admits. There will in the end be no error.
lines.plain: A simple offering: a jug of wine, a bowl of rice, plain clay vessels, passed in through a window. In hard times, simplicity and sincerity are enough. No blame.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the water of the defile not yet full, (so that it might flow away); but order will (soon) be brought about. There will be no error.
lines.plain: The water has not overflowed the pit; it only reaches the brim. Do not try to do more than is necessary. Getting out safely is enough.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject bound with cords of three strands or two strands, and placed in the thicket of thorns. But in three years he does not learn the course for him to pursue. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Bound with ropes and surrounded by thorns. You have lost your way and will need a long time to find it again. This is a serious difficulty.

hexagrams.name: The Clinging
hexagrams.core: a time of clarity and brightness, which lasts when it is connected to something that sustains it
hexagrams.now: Fire upon fire: brightness doubled. The Clinging describes light, clarity and awareness. Fire must cling to something in order to burn — wood, oil, a wick. Likewise, clarity depends on something to sustain it. The text promises success to firm correctness and advises caring for the cow — a symbol of docility and nourishment. Recognize what you depend on, and let your understanding be warm and steady, not frantic.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward greater clarity and insight. It will be important to recognize what you depend on and to keep your light steady.
avoid: Burning out from too much intensity
hexagrams.love: Bring warmth and understanding into the relationship. Clarify feelings honestly.
hexagrams.work: Clarity and vision are your strengths. Communicate them clearly.
hexagrams.self: Shed light on your situation. Identify what you truly depend on.
hexagrams.jung: The Clinging may symbolize consciousness itself — the light of awareness that depends on its connection to the unconscious for its fuel.
hexagrams.example: Gaining insight into a problem, a teacher inspiring students, or realizing how much you depend on a relationship.
hexagrams.judgment: Lî indicates that, (in regard to what it denotes), it will be advantageous to be firm and correct, and that thus there will be free course and success. Let (its subject) also nourish (a docility like that of) the cow, and there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram for) brightness, repeated, forms Lî. The great man, in accordance with this, cultivates more and more his brilliant (virtue), and diffuses its brightness over the four quarters (of the land).

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows one ready to move with confused steps. But he treads at the same time reverently, and there will be no mistake.
lines.plain: Footsteps going in many directions at once at the start of the day. In the first rush of activity, stay attentive and respectful, and you will avoid mistakes.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject in his place in yellow. There will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: A yellow light, the color of the center. Clarity combined with moderation brings great good fortune.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject in a position like that of the declining sun. Instead of playing on his instrument of earthenware, and singing to it, he utters the groans of an old man of eighty. There will be evil.
lines.plain: The light of the setting sun. People either sing and beat the drum or lament old age. Do not waste time on grief or forced gaiety; accept the cycles of life calmly.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the manner of its subject's coming. How abrupt it is, as with fire, with death, to be rejected (by all)!
lines.plain: A fire that flares up suddenly, burns out and is discarded. Abrupt intensity cannot last. Avoid acting violently or impulsively.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject as one with tears flowing in torrents, and groaning in sorrow. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Tears flowing, sighing and grief. Genuine sorrow and humility, especially in a high position, lead to good fortune.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows the king employing its subject in his punitive expeditions. Achieving admirable (merit), he breaks (only) the chiefs (of the rebels). Where his prisoners were not their associates, he does not punish. There will be no error.
lines.plain: The king goes out to correct wrongs. Punish only the leaders of a rebellion and spare the followers. Firm action should be fair and proportionate.

hexagrams.name: Influence
hexagrams.core: a time of mutual attraction and influence, when openness and humility create genuine connection
hexagrams.now: A lake on top of a mountain: the mountain receives and supports the water. Influence describes mutual attraction and the power of genuine feeling. The text says it brings success, and that taking a maiden in marriage brings good fortune. Real influence comes not from pressure, but from openness, sincerity and receptivity. When you are humble and genuine, people respond naturally.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward attraction and mutual influence. Openness and sincerity will create genuine connections.
hexagrams.love: Strong attraction or emotional connection. Let it develop with openness and respect.
hexagrams.work: Influence others by listening and responding sincerely.
hexagrams.self: Notice what moves you deeply. Your feelings are a guide.
hexagrams.jung: Influence may describe the mutual attraction of opposites — conscious and unconscious, masculine and feminine. In relationships it can reflect projection, as we see in others parts of ourselves.
hexagrams.example: Falling in love, finding an inspiring mentor, or forming a close friendship.
hexagrams.judgment: Hsien indicates that, (on the fulfilment of the conditions implied in it), there will be free course and success. Its advantageousness will depend on the being firm and correct, (as) in marrying a young lady. There will be good fortune.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain and above it that for (the waters of) a marsh form Hsien. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps his mind free from pre-occupation, and open to receive (the influences of) others.

lines.legge: The first six, divided, shows one moving his great toes.
lines.plain: Feeling begins in the big toe. An impulse is stirring, but nothing has happened yet. Notice it without acting on it.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows one moving the calves of his leg. There will be evil. If he abide (quiet in his place), there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Feeling moves the calves. Wanting to rush forward before you have thought things through leads to trouble. Waiting brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows one moving his thighs, and keeping close hold of those whom he follows. Going forward (in this way) will cause regret.
lines.plain: Feeling reaches the thighs, and you follow others or your impulses blindly. Moving on this basis will bring regret. Hold to your own judgement.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows that firm correctness whi.ch will lead to good fortune, and prevent all occasion for repentance. If its subject be unsettled in his movements, (only) his friends will follow his purpose.
lines.plain: Firm correctness brings good fortune and regret disappears. If your mind is restless and calculating, only close friends will follow you. Influence that comes from the heart spreads further.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows one moving the flesh along the spine above the heart. There will be no occasion for repentance.
lines.plain: Feeling in the muscles of the back, the part least moved by emotion. Your resolve is firm, but you remain largely unmoved. There is no regret, though little influence either.

lines.legge: The sixth six, divided, shows one moving his jaws and tongue.
lines.plain: Feeling reaches the jaws, cheeks and tongue. It turns into talk. Words alone do not move others; sincere action does.

hexagrams.name: Duration
hexagrams.core: a time of duration and perseverance, when lasting success comes from steady commitment that still adapts
hexagrams.now: Thunder and wind work together, enduring forces of nature. Duration describes perseverance and lasting commitment. The text says it brings success and no blame. Duration is not rigidity; like the seasons, it is constant movement within a stable pattern. Keep your commitments, stay true to your direction, and adapt your methods to changing circumstances.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a phase where consistency and long-term commitment become important.
do: Adapt your methods while keeping your direction
hexagrams.love: Long-term commitment and reliability are the foundation of trust.
hexagrams.work: Steady effort over time produces the strongest results.
hexagrams.self: Persist in what matters. Small daily actions build lasting change.
hexagrams.jung: Duration may suggest the stability of identity over time — the continuity of the Self beneath changing moods and circumstances.
hexagrams.example: A long marriage, a career built over decades, or a lifelong practice.
hexagrams.judgment: Hăng indicates successful progress and no error (in what it denotes). But the advantage will come from being firm and correct; and movement in any direction whatever will be advantageous.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) thunder and that for wind form Hăng. The superior man, in accordance with this, stands firm, and does not change his method (of operation).

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject deeply (desirous) of long continuance. Even with firm correctness there will be evil; there will be no advantage in any way.
lines.plain: Insisting on permanence too early and too deeply. Demanding lasting results from the start leads to trouble. Let durability grow over time.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows all occasion for repentance disappearing.
lines.plain: Regret disappears. By staying in the middle path, you avoid excess and find steady footing.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows one who does not continuously maintain his virtue. There are those who will impute this to him as a disgrace. However firm he may be, there will be ground for regret.
lines.plain: Not keeping your character consistent. Changing your values with every situation brings disgrace and regret.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows a field where there is no game.
lines.plain: Hunting in a field where there is no game. Persistence in the wrong place brings nothing. Check whether you are aiming in the right direction.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject continuously maintaining the virtue indicated by it. In a wife this will be fortunate; in a husband, evil.
lines.plain: Constancy in following, which is right for someone in a supporting role. But someone who must lead needs to act on their own judgement, not mere compliance. Know which role you hold.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject exciting himself to long continuance. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Restlessness as a permanent state. Constantly stirring things up without settling leads to misfortune.

hexagrams.name: Retreat
hexagrams.core: a time to step back from an unfavourable situation, withdrawing with dignity to preserve your strength
hexagrams.now: Mountain beneath heaven: the mountain rises, but heaven withdraws before it. Retreat describes a time when opposing forces are growing stronger and continued engagement would waste your energy. The traditional text says that success lies in withdrawal, and that only in small matters is it still useful to persist. Retreat is not defeat. It is a deliberate choice to create distance, keep your dignity and preserve your strength for a better moment. The Image adds an important detail: the wise person keeps petty people at a distance, not with hatred, but with calm reserve.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time when stepping back is wiser than pushing on. Creating distance, without bitterness, can protect your energy and independence.
do: Recognize when continued effort is no longer productive
Keep your dignity and your options open
avoid: Staying too long out of pride or habit
Leaving in anger or creating enemies
hexagrams.love: If a relationship is draining or one-sided, some distance may help both people see clearly. Step back with kindness, not punishment.
hexagrams.work: A project, role or negotiation may no longer be worth the cost. Plan an orderly exit or reduce your involvement without burning bridges.
hexagrams.self: Protect your energy. Saying no to some things is a way of saying yes to yourself.
hexagrams.jung: Psychologically, Retreat may describe the healthy withdrawal of energy from an outer situation that no longer holds meaning, so that it can turn inward and be renewed. Jung saw such periods of introversion as a natural phase of growth, not a failure.
hexagrams.example: Leaving a job with a toxic culture, stepping back from a family argument, or ending a commitment that has become an obligation without purpose.
hexagrams.judgment: Thun indicates successful progress (in its circumstances). To a small extent it will (still) be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the sky and below it that for a mountain form Thun. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps small men at a distance, not by showing that he hates them, but by his own dignified gravity.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows a retiring tail. The position is perilous. No movement in any direction should be made.
lines.plain: The tail end of a retreat: you are the last to leave and the most exposed. This is dangerous. Do not start anything new now; simply get out of harm's way quietly.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject holding (his purpose) fast as if by a (thong made from the) hide of a yellow ox, which cannot be broken.
lines.plain: Held fast as if by a strap of yellow oxhide that cannot be broken. A firm commitment or loyalty holds you in place. Here, staying true to what binds you is right, even while others withdraw.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows one retiring but bound,--to his distress and peril. (If he were to deal with his binders as in) nourishing a servant or concubine, it would be fortunate for him.
lines.plain: A retreat that is held back by ties and obligations, which is stressful and dangerous. Treat the people who hold you back kindly, as you would care for those who depend on you, and the situation can turn out well.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject retiring notwithstanding his likings. In a superior man this will lead to good fortune; a small man cannot attain to this.
lines.plain: Voluntary retreat, even from something you like. A mature person can let go of what they enjoy when the time is right and finds good fortune in it. Someone ruled by desire cannot.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject retiring in an admirable way. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: A friendly, well-timed retreat. Leaving at the right moment, with courtesy and firm purpose, brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject retiring in a noble way. It will be advantageous in every respect.
lines.plain: A cheerful, free retreat. You leave without regret, resentment or entanglement, and everything works out well.

hexagrams.name: The Power of the Great
hexagrams.core: a time of great strength and momentum, which succeeds only when power is guided by what is right
hexagrams.now: Thunder high in heaven: strength in motion. The Power of the Great describes a time when you have energy, confidence and influence. The text says firm correctness is what makes this favourable. Real strength includes self-control. The Image advises not taking any step that is not in accordance with what is proper. Power without restraint can run into walls, like a ram that gets its horns stuck in a fence. Use your strength for what is right and know when not to push.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward greater strength and momentum. The challenge will be to use power wisely and with restraint.
do: Use your strength for good purposes
hexagrams.love: Your strength can be protective and reassuring, but make sure it does not become controlling.
hexagrams.work: You have influence and momentum. Use it fairly, and do not overreach.
hexagrams.self: Feel your strength, then choose to direct it carefully.
hexagrams.jung: The Power of the Great may describe a surge of energy from the unconscious that empowers the ego. The risk is identification with power, an inflation that loses sight of limits.
hexagrams.example: Getting a big promotion, winning an argument, or feeling unusually energetic and confident.
hexagrams.judgment: Tâ Kwang indicates that (under the conditions which it symbolises) it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) heaven and above it that for thunder form Tâ Kwang. The superior man, in accordance with this, does not take a step which is not according to propriety.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject manifesting his strength in his toes. But advance will lead to evil,--most certainly.
lines.plain: Strength in the toes: pushing forward from the very bottom with no real position. Advancing now leads to misfortune. Wait.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows that with firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Firm correctness brings good fortune. Your strength is well balanced; keep it that way.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows, in the case of a small man, one using all his strength; and in the case of a superior man, one whose rule is not to do so. Even with firm correctness the position would be perilous. (The exercise of strength in it might be compared to the case of) a ram butting against a fence, and getting his horns entangled.
lines.plain: A petty person uses force; a superior person does not, knowing it is dangerous. A ram that butts a fence gets its horns caught. Do not force things.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows (a case in which) firm correctness leads to good fortune, and occasion for repentance disappears. (We see) the fence opened without the horns being entangled. The strength is like that in the wheel-spokes of a large waggon.
lines.plain: Firm correctness brings good fortune and regret vanishes. The fence opens and the horns are free. Strength is like the axle of a big cart: steady, quiet power that carries you forward.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows one who loses his ram(-like strength) in the ease of his position. (But) there will be no occasion for repentance.
lines.plain: Losing the ram's stubbornness with ease. Letting go of the urge to force brings no regret.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided, shows (one who may be compared to) the ram butting against the fence, and unable either to retreat, or to advance as he would fain do. There will not be advantage in any respect; but if he realise the difficulty (of his position), there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: A ram butts the fence and cannot go forward or back. Nothing furthers. Recognizing the difficulty brings good fortune in the end.

hexagrams.name: Progress
hexagrams.core: a time of rapid, easy progress, like the sun rising over the earth, in which clarity and good conduct bring recognition
hexagrams.now: The sun rises over the earth. Progress describes a time of steady advancement and recognition. The traditional text pictures a prince honoured with many horses by the king and received three times in a single day. Your efforts are noticed and things move forward. The Image advises the wise person to make their own bright virtue shine. Progress here depends on clarity and on serving something larger than yourself.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward progress and recognition. Clarity and generosity will help you advance.
do: Let your strengths and good qualities be seen
Serve the people who support you
hexagrams.love: The relationship can grow openly and joyfully. Share your progress with your partner.
hexagrams.work: A good time for advancement, visibility and recognition.
hexagrams.self: Let your best qualities shine. Growth comes naturally when you are clear about who you are.
hexagrams.jung: Progress, the rising sun, may symbolize expanding consciousness. As awareness grows, the ego can make progress, provided it remains connected to the deeper Self.
hexagrams.example: Getting a promotion, receiving public recognition, or making steady progress in learning.
hexagrams.judgment: In Žin we see a prince who secures the tranquillity (of the people) presented on that account with numerous horses (by the king), and three times in a day received at interviews.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for the bright (sun) coming forth above it form Žin. The superior man, according to this, gives himself to make more brilliant his bright virtue.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows one wishing to advance, and (at the same time) kept back. Let him be firm and correct, and there will be good fortune. If trust be not reposed in him, let him maintain a large and generous mind, and there will be no error.
lines.plain: Progressing, but held back. Stay correct and calm. If others do not yet trust you, stay generous and relaxed; there is no mistake.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject with the appearance of advancing, and yet of being sorrowful. If he be firm and correct, there will be good fortune. He will receive this great blessing from his grandmother.
lines.plain: Progressing, but feeling sorrowful. Stay firm. Great blessing will come from a motherly or caring figure.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject trusted by all (around him). All occasion for repentance will disappear.
lines.plain: Everyone agrees with you. Support from others makes regret disappear.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with the appearance of advancing, but like a marmot. However firm and correct he may be, the position is one of peril.
lines.plain: Progressing like a squirrel: clinging to position and grasping. This is dangerous even if correct.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows how all occasion for repentance disappears (from its subject). (But) let him not concern himself about whether he shall fail or succeed. To advance will be fortunate, and in every way advantageous.
lines.plain: Regret disappears. Do not worry about gain or loss; going forward brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows one advancing his horns. But he only uses them to punish the (rebellious people of his own) city. The position is perilous, but there will be good fortune. (Yet) however firm and correct he may be, there will be occasion for regret.
lines.plain: Progressing with the horns, using force only to set your own house in order. There is danger, but good fortune and no blame. Continuing this way brings humiliation.

hexagrams.name: Darkening of the Light
hexagrams.core: a dark time in which you protect your inner light by being discreet and keeping your integrity
hexagrams.now: The sun has sunk beneath the earth. Darkening of the Light describes a time of adversity, when good qualities are not recognized and may even be resented. The text says it is advantageous to be firm and correct in difficulty. Sometimes the wisest course is to hide your light — to stay discreet, protect yourself and keep your integrity quietly, as the Image says, veiling your brightness while still remaining bright within. Darkness does not last forever.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a difficult or unappreciative environment, where discretion and inner steadiness protect you.
do: Be discreet and do not provoke
hexagrams.love: Be patient through difficult times. Protect what is precious between you.
hexagrams.work: In a hostile or unfair environment, keep a low profile and protect your reputation.
hexagrams.self: Hold on to your inner values even when they are not reflected around you.
hexagrams.jung: Darkening of the Light may describe a time when consciousness is overwhelmed by the shadow, depression or outer difficulties. The task is to keep a spark of awareness alive through the darkness.
hexagrams.example: Working under an unfair boss, living through a period of depression, or enduring a time of injustice.
hexagrams.judgment: Ming Î indicates that (in the circumstances which it denotes) it will be advantageous to realise the difficulty (of the position), and maintain firm correctness.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for the bright (sun) entering within it form Ming Î. The superior man, in accordance with this, conducts his management of men;--he shows his intelligence by keeping it obscured.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, flying, but with drooping wings. When the superior man (is revolving) his going away, he may be for three days without eating. Wherever he goes, the people there may speak (derisively of him).
lines.plain: Darkening of the light while flying: the wings droop. You may have to go without comfort for a while. People may misunderstand you, but persevere.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, wounded in the left thigh. He saves himself by the strength of a (swift) horse; and is fortunate.
lines.plain: Wounded in the left thigh. Help comes from a strong horse. Use whatever support you can; there is good fortune.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, hunting in the south, and taking the great chief (of the darkness). He should not be eager to make (all) correct (at once).
lines.plain: During a hunt in the south, the leader of darkness is captured. Change cannot be rushed, but it is now possible.

lines.legge: The fourth six, divided, shows its subject (just) entered into the left side of the belly (of the dark land). (But) he is able to carry out the mind appropriate (in the condition indicated by) Ming Î, quitting the gate and courtyard (of the lord of darkness).
lines.plain: Entering the left side of the belly, understanding the heart of the darkening, and then leaving through the gate. Knowing the true situation, you withdraw.

lines.legge: The fifth six, divided, shows how the count of Kî fulfilled the condition indicated by Ming Î. It will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
lines.plain: Prince Ji's darkening of the light: he hid his wisdom to survive under a tyrant. Firmness furthers.

lines.legge: The sixth six, divided, shows the case where there is no light, but (only) obscurity. (Its subject) had at first ascended to (the top of) the sky; his future shall be to go into the earth.
lines.plain: Not light but darkness. First it climbs to heaven, then it plunges into the earth. Darkness destroys itself.

hexagrams.name: The Family
hexagrams.core: a time to strengthen close relationships and the home, where clear roles and sincere words create order
hexagrams.now: Wind comes forth from fire: influence spreads outward from the hearth. The Family describes the inner circle of life — home, family, close relationships — and the clear roles and mutual respect that make it work. The text says it is advantageous for the woman of the household to be firm and correct. In modern terms, the hexagram emphasizes responsibility, consistency and sincere words that are backed by actions. When the family is in order, the wider world is set in order too.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a focus on home, family and close relationships, where clear roles and loving discipline are needed.
do: Make your words match your actions
hexagrams.love: Commitment and shared responsibilities strengthen the relationship. Be reliable.
hexagrams.work: Treat the team like a family: clear roles, mutual respect and consistency.
hexagrams.self: Look at the patterns you learned at home. Which ones support you?
hexagrams.jung: The Family may point to the family complexes that shape the personality. It invites reflection on the roles and patterns inherited from parents and their effects on present relationships.
hexagrams.example: Setting new household routines, resolving family tensions, or building trust in a small team.
hexagrams.judgment: For (the realisation of what is taught in) Kiâ Zăn, (or for the regulation of the family), what is most advantageous is that the wife be firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) fire, and that for wind coming forth from it, form Kiâ Zăn. The superior man, in accordance with this, orders his words according to (the truth of) things, and his conduct so that it is uniformly consistent.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject establishing restrictive regulations in his household Occasion for repentance will disappear.
lines.plain: Firm boundaries within the family. Clear rules from the start prevent later regret.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject taking nothing on herself, but in her central place attending to the preparation of the food. Through her firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: She does not follow her whims, but attends to the household. Steady care brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject (treating) the members of the household with stern severity. There will be occasion for repentance, there will be peril, (but) there will (also) be good fortune. If the wife and children were to be smirking and chattering, in the end there would be occasion for regret.
lines.plain: When family members are treated too harshly, there is regret, but still good fortune; when they giggle and jest without restraint, humiliation follows. Strictness is better than indulgence.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject enriching the family. There will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: She is the treasure of the house. Great good fortune.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the influence of the king extending to his family. There need be no anxiety; there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: As a king approaches his family, there is no fear. Good fortune. Lead with love.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity and arrayed in majesty. In the end there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Sincerity and dignity bring good fortune in the end.

hexagrams.name: Opposition
hexagrams.core: a time of opposition and misunderstanding, when small steps toward understanding can still succeed
hexagrams.now: Fire above, lake below: fire rises and water sinks, moving in opposite directions. Opposition describes estrangement, misunderstanding or different perspectives. The text says that in small matters there is good fortune. Large, joint undertakings may not work now, but small acts of understanding can. Respect differences. The Image advises the wise person to recognize what he has in common with others while keeping what makes him distinct.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward differences or misunderstandings. Small steps toward understanding will be more effective than big gestures.
do: Look for small points of agreement
hexagrams.love: You may see things differently. Small gestures of understanding can bridge the gap.
hexagrams.work: Not everyone will agree. Achieve small wins and avoid big, risky collaborations now.
hexagrams.self: Accept that you have conflicting feelings or that others see you differently.
hexagrams.jung: Opposition may describe the polarity of opposites within the psyche. The tension of opposites can lead to new understanding when it is held consciously rather than resolved too quickly.
hexagrams.example: A disagreement with a partner, different views within a team, or a family member who sees things very differently.
hexagrams.judgment: Khwei indicates that, (notwithstanding the condition of things which it denotes), in small matters there will (still) be good success.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) fire above, and that for (the waters of) a marsh below, form Khwei. The superior man, in accordance with this, where there is a general agreement, yet admits diversity.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows that (to its subject) occasion for repentance will disappear. He has lost his horses, but let him not seek for them;--they will return of themselves. Should he meet with bad men, he will not err (in communicating with them).
lines.plain: Regret disappears. If you lose your horse, do not run after it; it will return by itself. When you meet unpleasant people, be courteous.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject happening to meet with his lord in a bye-passage. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Meeting your lord in a narrow street. An unexpected encounter can resolve a misunderstanding. No blame.

lines.legge: In the third SIX, divided, we see one whose carriage is dragged back, while the oxen in it are pushed back, and he is himself subjected to the shaving of his head and the cutting off of his nose. There is no good beginning, but there will be a good end.
lines.plain: The cart is dragged back, the oxen halted, the man's hair and nose cut off. A bad beginning, but a good end.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (But) he meets with the good man (represented by the first line), and they blend their sincere desires together. The position is one of peril, but there will be no mistake.
lines.plain: Isolated through opposition, you meet a like-minded person and trust each other. Danger, but no blame.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows that (to its subject) occasion for repentance will disappear. With his relative (and minister he unites closely and readily) as if he were biting through a piece of skin. When he goes forward (with this help), what error can there be?
lines.plain: Regret disappears. Your companion bites through the wrapping. Going forward together brings no blame.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (In the subject of the third line, he seems to) see a pig bearing on its back a load of mud, (or fancies) there is a carriage full of ghosts. He first bends his bow against him, and afterwards unbends it, (for he discovers) that he is not an assailant to injure, but a near relative. Going forward, he shall meet with (genial) rain, and there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Isolated through opposition, you see a pig covered with mud, a cart full of devils. You draw your bow, then put it down. It is not a robber but a suitor. Misunderstandings dissolve, like rain clearing the air.

hexagrams.name: Obstruction
hexagrams.core: a time of obstruction, when the wise response is to pause, reflect, seek help and improve yourself
hexagrams.now: Water on the mountain: danger ahead and a steep slope behind. Obstruction describes a situation where the way forward is blocked. The traditional text says that the southwest (the direction of easy, open country) is favourable and the northeast (steep mountains) is not, and that it furthers you to see the great man. In plain terms, do not keep charging at the obstacle. Step back, seek help, and use the obstacle as a reason to examine and improve yourself.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward obstacles. Pausing, seeking help and improving yourself will be more effective than forcing your way.
do: Use the obstacle to improve yourself
hexagrams.love: If you feel blocked, look at your own role first. Ask for help or counselling if needed.
hexagrams.work: A project may hit obstacles. Regroup, seek advice and change your approach.
hexagrams.self: The obstacle may be teaching you something. Turn inward and ask what.
hexagrams.jung: Obstruction may symbolize an inner obstacle — a complex or resistance that blocks psychological growth. Rather than fighting it, one can turn inward to understand it.
hexagrams.example: A delayed project, a stalled career, or a personal problem that does not seem to move.
hexagrams.judgment: In (the state indicated by) Kien advantage will be found in the south-west, and the contrary in the north-east. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man. (In these circumstances), with firmness and correctness, there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and above it that for water, form Kien. The superior man, in accordance with this, turns round (and examines) himself, and cultivates his virtue.

lines.legge: From the first SIX, divided, we learn that advance (on the part of its subject) will lead to (greater) difficulties, while remaining stationary will afford ground for praise.
lines.plain: Going forward leads into difficulty; holding back earns praise. Wait for a better moment rather than pushing into the obstacle.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows the minister of the king struggling with difficulty on difficulty, and not with a view to his own advantage.
lines.plain: Like a loyal servant of the king, you meet difficulty upon difficulty, and not through any fault or selfish aim of your own. Keep working for the greater good; you are not to blame.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and returns (to his former associates).
lines.plain: Going forward would only make the obstacle worse, so you turn back to the people who rely on you. Returning to your own circle is right for now.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and unites (with the subject of the line above).
lines.plain: Going forward leads to difficulty; staying back lets you join forces with others. Build alliances before you try again.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject struggling with the greatest difficulties, while friends are coming to help him.
lines.plain: In the middle of the greatest difficulty, friends arrive to help. When you hold to your purpose, support comes when it is most needed.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject going forward, (only to increase) the difficulties, while his remaining stationary will be (productive of) great (merit). There will be good fortune, and it will be advantageous to meet with the great man.
lines.plain: Pressing on would only add to the trouble; staying and working with others brings great achievement and good fortune. Seek out a wise and capable person.

hexagrams.name: Deliverance
hexagrams.core: a time of release after tension, when problems can be resolved quickly and old grievances forgiven
hexagrams.now: Thunder and rain: the storm breaks and the air clears. Deliverance describes the release of tension after a difficult period. The text says the southwest is favourable, and that where nothing more needs to be done, returning to normal brings good fortune; where something still needs doing, acting quickly brings good fortune. The Image advises the wise person to forgive mistakes and pardon misdeeds. Let go of what is over, finish what is necessary and return to normal life.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward release and relief. Resolve what remains quickly, forgive and return to ordinary life.
hexagrams.love: Clear the air and forgive. A fresh start is possible.
hexagrams.work: Tie up loose ends quickly and move on. Do not dwell on past mistakes.
hexagrams.self: Release tension, rest and let go of what is over.
hexagrams.jung: Deliverance may describe the release of psychic tension after a complex has been made conscious. The energy bound up in conflict becomes free for life again.
hexagrams.example: The end of an exam period, resolving a dispute, or recovering after a crisis.
hexagrams.judgment: In (the state indicated by) Kieh advantage will be found in the south-west. If no (further) operations be called for, there will be good fortune in coming back (to the old conditions). If some operations be called for, there will be good fortune in the early conducting of them.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) thunder and that for rain, with these phenomena in a state of manifestation, form Kieh. The superior man, in accordance with this, forgives errors, and deals gently with crimes.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows that its subject will commit no error.
lines.plain: The tension has eased and the problem is resolved. Rest quietly; there is no blame.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject catch, in hunting, three foxes, and obtain the yellow (= golden) arrows. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Catching three foxes in the field and gaining a yellow arrow. You remove sly, deceptive influences while staying straight and balanced yourself. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows a porter with his burden, (yet) riding in a carriage. He will (only) tempt robbers to attack him. However firm and correct he may (try to) be, there will be cause for regret.
lines.plain: A porter carrying a load while riding in a fine carriage invites robbers. Claiming a position you have not earned attracts trouble. Be honest about where you stand.

lines.legge: (To the subject of) the fourth NINE, undivided, (it is said), 'Remove your toes. Friends will (then) come, between you and whom there will be mutual confidence.'
lines.plain: Free yourself from a dependent or unworthy connection, as one shakes off something clinging to the toe. Then a true friend can come, and trust grows between you.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows (its subject), the superior man (= the ruler), executing his function of removing (whatever is injurious to the idea of the hexagram), in which case there will he good fortune, and confidence in him will be shown even by the small men.
lines.plain: Only a person of real character can bring this release by removing what is harmful. Good fortune; even skeptical or petty people are convinced by the result.

lines.legge: In the sixth SIX, divided, we see a feudal prince (with his bow) shooting at a falcon on the top of a high wall, and hitting it. (The effect of his action) will be in every way advantageous.
lines.plain: A prince shoots at a hawk perched on a high wall and brings it down. Removing the last, well-placed obstacle frees everything. All is favourable.

hexagrams.name: Decrease
