hexagrams.core: a time of decrease, when reducing excess, simplifying and giving sincerely can strengthen what matters most
hexagrams.now: A lake at the foot of a mountain: the lake gives up water to the mountain, which becomes greener. Decrease describes a time when something must be reduced, given up or simplified. The text says that if decrease is combined with sincerity, it brings great good fortune, and that even two small bowls are enough for a sacrifice. Less can be more. Cutting back on excess, controlling anger and desire, and giving to what deserves support can strengthen what is essential.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a period of reduction or simplification. Sincerity and wise sacrifice will make it fruitful.
hexagrams.love: Let go of unnecessary demands or expectations. Simple sincerity is enough.
hexagrams.work: Cut costs or simplify processes. Focus resources where they matter most.
hexagrams.self: Practise restraint and simplicity. Ask what you can let go of.
hexagrams.jung: Decrease may describe the reduction of ego-demands so that something deeper can grow. Sacrificing a one-sided attitude can make space for the Self.
hexagrams.example: Reducing spending, decluttering, cutting back on commitments, or giving time to others.
hexagrams.judgment: In (what is denoted by) Sun, if there be sincerity (in him who employs it), there will be great good fortune:--freedom from error; firmness and correctness that can be maintained; and advantage in every movement that shall be made. In what shall this (sincerity in the exercise of Sun) be employed? (Even) in sacrifice two baskets of grain, (though there be nothing else), may be presented.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain and beneath it that for the waters of a marsh form Sun. The superior man, in accordance with this, restrains his wrath and represses his desires.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject suspending his own affairs, and hurrying away (to help the subject of the fourth line). He will commit no error, but let him consider how far he should contribute of what is his (for the other).
lines.plain: When your own work is done, hurry to help others. That is right, but think carefully about how much you can give without depleting yourself.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows that it will be advantageous for its subject to maintain a firm correctness, and that action on his part will be evil. He can give increase (to his correlate) without taking from himself
lines.plain: Hold steady and correct; rushing into action now would bring misfortune. Sometimes you help others most by not diminishing yourself.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows how of three men walking together, the number is diminished by one; and how one, walking, finds his friend.
lines.plain: When three travel together, one is lost; when one travels alone, he finds a companion. Groups of three tend to split; real closeness forms in pairs.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject diminishing the ailment under which he labours by making (the subject of the first line) hasten (to his help), and make him glad. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Reducing your own faults makes others come to you gladly. Letting go of what weighs on you brings joy and no blame.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows parties adding to (the stores of) its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells, and accepting no refusal. There will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: Someone adds to your fortune with a gift of great value that cannot be refused, like ten pairs of precious tortoise shells. Great good fortune comes without being sought.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject giving increase to others without taking from himself. There will be no error. With firm correctness there will be good fortune. There will be advantage in every movement that shall be made. He will find ministers more than can be counted by their clans.
lines.plain: You increase others without taking anything from yourself. No blame; staying firm brings good fortune, and people gather to help in a cause that serves everyone.

hexagrams.name: Increase
hexagrams.core: a time of increase and opportunity, when generosity from above enriches those below and bold action is favoured
hexagrams.now: Wind and thunder strengthen each other. Increase describes a time of growth and benefit, when what is above gives to what is below. The text says it furthers you to undertake something and to cross the great water — this is a time for bold action. The Image advises the wise person to imitate the good when they see it and correct their faults when they have them. Use this time of growth for real improvement and shared benefit.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward growth and opportunity. Generosity and bold, beneficial action will be supported.
do: Improve yourself by learning from good examples
hexagrams.love: Give generously and support each other's growth.
hexagrams.work: A good time to expand, invest and take on ambitious projects.
hexagrams.self: Grow by imitating good examples and correcting faults.
hexagrams.jung: Increase may describe a flow of energy from the unconscious that enriches consciousness — new insights, creativity and vitality.
hexagrams.example: Getting resources for a project, receiving help from a mentor, or seeing a business grow.
hexagrams.judgment: Yî indicates that (in the state which it denotes) there will be advantage in every movement which shall be undertaken, that it will be advantageous (even) to cross the great stream.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) wind and that for thunder form Yî. The superior man, in accordance with this, when he sees what is good, moves towards it; and when he sees his errors, he turns from them.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows that it will be advantageous for its subject in his position to make a great movement. If it be greatly fortunate, no blame will be imputed to him.
lines.plain: You are supported to undertake something significant. Use this help for a great, worthwhile effort; then there will be great good fortune and no blame.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows parties adding to the stores of its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells whose oracles cannot be opposed. Let him persevere in being firm and correct, and there will be good fortune. Let the king, (having the virtues thus distinguished), employ them in presenting his offerings to God, and there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Someone adds to your fortune with a valuable gift you cannot refuse. Stay constant and sincere, and keep your gains in service of something higher. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows increase given to its subject by means of what is evil, so that he shall (be led to good), and be without blame. Let him be sincere and pursue the path of the Mean, (so shall he secure the recognition of the ruler, like) an officer who announces himself to his prince by the symbol of his rank.
lines.plain: Increase comes even through misfortune, which becomes a test that strengthens you. Stay sincere, keep to the middle path and report honestly to those above you; then there is no blame.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject pursuing the due course. His advice to his prince is followed. He can with advantage be relied on in such a movement as that of removing the capital.
lines.plain: Walking the middle path, you advise those in authority and they follow. You can be trusted with large changes, even something as big as moving a capital.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with sincere heart seeking to benefit (all below). There need be no question about it; the result will be great good fortune. (All below) will with sincere heart acknowledge his goodness.
lines.plain: A sincere, kind heart that seeks to benefit others has no need to ask whether it is right. Great good fortune; people recognize your goodness.

lines.legge: In the sixth NINE, undivided, we see one to whose increase none will contribute, while many will seek to assail him. He observes no regular rule in the ordering of his heart. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Taking from others instead of giving, without any steady principle. People stop supporting you and may even attack. This brings misfortune.

hexagrams.name: Breakthrough
hexagrams.core: a time to make a decisive breakthrough by openly naming what is wrong, without resorting to violence or force
hexagrams.now: The lake has risen to heaven: tension builds until it breaks through. Breakthrough describes a time when something must be resolved decisively. The text says you must announce the matter openly at the king's court and be truthful, aware of the danger involved. It does not favour taking up arms. Problems should be confronted openly and honestly, without aggression. Courage and clarity, not force, bring the breakthrough.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a decisive breakthrough. Openness, honesty and courage will be needed.
do: Name the problem openly and honestly
hexagrams.love: Speak openly about what needs to change. Honesty can break through a stalemate.
hexagrams.work: Make the decision that has been delayed. Communicate it clearly.
hexagrams.self: Face the truth about a situation you have avoided.
hexagrams.jung: Breakthrough may describe the moment when a long-repressed insight bursts into consciousness. The ego must face it openly rather than suppress it again.
hexagrams.example: Calling out unethical behaviour, ending an unhealthy situation, or making a decision you have long postponed.
hexagrams.judgment: Kwâi requires (in him who would fulfil its meaning) the exhibition (of the culprit's guilt) in the royal court, and a sincere and earnest appeal (for sympathy and support), with a consciousness of the peril (involved in cutting off the criminal). He should (also) make announcement in his own city, and show that it will not be well to have recourse at once to arms. (In this way) there will be advantage in whatever he shall go forward to.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) heaven and that for the waters of a marsh mounting above it form Kwâi. The superior man, in accordance with this, bestows emolument on those below him, and dislikes allowing his gifts to accumulate (undispensed).

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject in (the pride of) strength advancing with his toes. He goes forward, but will not succeed. There will be ground for blame.
lines.plain: Striding forward full of pride in your strength, you are not equal to the task. Overconfidence at the start leads to mistakes.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject full of apprehension and appealing (for sympathy and help). Late at night hostile measures may be (taken against him), but he need not be anxious about them.
lines.plain: Calling out a warning and staying alert. Even if there is danger at night, you need not fear because you are prepared.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject (about to advance) with strong (and determined) looks. There will be evil. (But) the superior man, bent on cutting off (the criminal), will walk alone and encounter the rain, (till he be hated by his proper associates) as if he were contaminated (by the others). (In the end) there will be no blame against him.
lines.plain: Showing determination in your face invites trouble. The wise person stays resolved, walks alone through the rain, gets soaked and is misunderstood, but is not to blame.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped, and who walks slowly and with difficulty. (If he could act) like. a sheep led (after its companions), occasion for repentance would disappear. But though he hear these words, he will not believe them.
lines.plain: Like someone who cannot sit or walk comfortably, you are restless. If you allowed yourself to be guided, regret would disappear, but you will not listen to advice.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows (the small men like) a bed of purslain, which ought to be uprooted with the utmost determination. (The subject of the line having such determination), his action, in harmony with his central position, will lead to no error or blame.
lines.plain: Weeds must be pulled out firmly, roots and all. Deal decisively with the problem while staying balanced in your conduct. No blame.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject without any (helpers) on whom to call. His end will be evil.
lines.plain: No one to call for help. A problem that is not fully resolved returns. In the end, misfortune follows.

hexagrams.name: Coming to Meet
hexagrams.core: an unexpected encounter or influence, which can be welcomed briefly but should not be allowed to take control
hexagrams.now: Wind under heaven: something blows in from outside. Coming to Meet describes an unexpected encounter — a new person, opportunity or influence. The text pictures a bold woman and advises not to marry such a woman: do not give a strong, unbalanced influence too much power. A small influence that seems harmless can grow strong if you are not careful. Meet new things openly, but with discernment.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward an unexpected encounter or influence. Meet it with openness, but stay discerning.
avoid: Letting a small influence take control
hexagrams.love: An attractive new connection may come. Enjoy it, but do not rush into commitment.
hexagrams.work: New opportunities appear. Evaluate them carefully before you commit.
hexagrams.self: Notice a temptation or habit that seems small but might grow.
hexagrams.jung: Coming to Meet may describe an unexpected encounter with a part of the unconscious — often the anima or animus — that is fascinating but potentially overwhelming. It needs to be integrated, not obeyed.
hexagrams.example: A charming new acquaintance, a tempting offer, or a habit that starts small.
hexagrams.judgment: Kâu shows a female who is bold and strong. It will not be good to marry (such) a female.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) wind and that for the sky above it form Kâu. The sovereign, in accordance with this, delivers his charges, and promulgates his announcements throughout the four quarters (of the kingdom).

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows how its subject should be kept (like a carriage) tied and fastened to a metal drag, in which case with firm correctness there will be good fortune. (But) if he move in any direction, evil will appear. He will be (like) a lean pig, which is sure to keep jumping about.
lines.plain: Stop it with a bronze brake. A small but dangerous influence should be checked firmly at the start; if it is allowed to run loose, like a restless pig, it brings trouble.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject with a wallet of fish. There will be no error. But it will not be well to let (the subject of the first line) go forward to the guests.
lines.plain: There is a fish in the basket. Keep this influence contained and under your care. Do not pass it on to others. No blame.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped so that he walks with difficulty. The position is perilous, but there will be no great error.
lines.plain: Like someone who cannot sit or walk comfortably, you feel uneasy and indecisive. There is danger, but no great mistake if you stay aware.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with his wallet, but no fish in it. This will give rise to evil.
lines.plain: The basket is empty; there is no fish. By keeping your distance from ordinary people, you lose their support. This leads to misfortune.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, (shows its subject as) a medlar tree overspreading the gourd (beneath it). If he keep his brilliant qualities concealed, (a good issue) will descend (as) from Heaven.
lines.plain: A melon sheltered under the leaves of a willow. Keep your good qualities modest and hidden, and success will come as if from heaven.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject receiving others on his horns. There will be occasion for regret, but there will be no error.
lines.plain: Meeting others with your horns. Being too aloof and confrontational brings regret, but no great blame.

hexagrams.name: Gathering Together
hexagrams.core: a time of gathering together around a common center, which needs leadership, sincerity and preparation
hexagrams.now: The lake over the earth: waters gather. Gathering Together describes the assembling of people around a common purpose. The text mentions the king approaching his temple, seeing the great man, and making great offerings. Gathering works best around a strong, sincere center. The Image warns that when many people gather, conflict can also arise, so prepare and stay alert.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time of gathering and community. Leadership, shared purpose and preparation will be important.
do: Gather people around a shared purpose
hexagrams.love: Family gatherings or shared commitments may strengthen your bond.
hexagrams.work: Bring people together for a common goal. Plan well and lead clearly.
hexagrams.self: Gather your inner resources and focus on what really matters.
hexagrams.jung: Gathering Together may describe the integration of scattered psychic contents around a central focus — the Self.
hexagrams.example: Organizing a reunion, starting a community group, or bringing a team together for a project.
hexagrams.judgment: In (the state denoted by) Žhui, the king will repair to his ancestral temple. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man; and then there will be progress and success, though the advantage must come through firm correctness. The use of great victims will conduce to good fortune; and in whatever direction movement is made, it will be advantageous.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing the) earth and that for the waters of a marsh raised above it form Žhui. The superior man, in accordance with this, has his weapons of war put in good repair, to be prepared against unforeseen contingencies.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject with a sincere desire (for union), but unable to carry it out, so that disorder is brought into the sphere of his union. If he cry out (for help to his proper correlate), all at once (his tears) will give place to smiles. He need not mind (the temporary difficulty); as he goes forward, there will be no error.
lines.plain: You sincerely want to join with others, but cannot carry it through, which causes confusion. If you call out for help, tears turn into smiles. Do not worry; go ahead.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject led forward (by his correlate). There will be good fortune, and freedom from error. There is entire sincerity, and in that case (even the small offerings of) the vernal sacrifice are acceptable.
lines.plain: Being drawn into the gathering by the right person brings good fortune. With sincerity, even a small offering is acceptable.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject striving after union and seeming to sigh, yet nowhere finding any advantage. If he go forward, he will not err, though there may be some small cause for regret.
lines.plain: Wanting to belong, but sighing because nothing works out. Going forward is still not a mistake, even if there is some small regret.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject in such a state that, if he be greatly fortunate, he will receive no blame.
lines.plain: Great good fortune is needed for this position to be without blame. Make sure your role in the group is earned and serves everyone.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the union (of all) under its subject in the place of dignity. There will be no error. If any do not have confidence in him, let him see to it that (his virtue) be great, long-continued, and firmly correct, and all occasion for repentance will disappear.
lines.plain: You are at the center of the gathering. If some do not yet trust you, keep developing lasting, firm integrity, and regret will disappear.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject sighing and weeping; but there will be no error.
lines.plain: Sighing and weeping because union has not been achieved. Sincere sorrow about this is not a mistake; it can open the way to reconciliation.

hexagrams.name: Pushing Upward
hexagrams.core: a time of steady upward growth, like a plant pushing through the earth, achieved through patient effort
hexagrams.now: Wood grows within the earth: a plant pushes steadily upward. Pushing Upward describes gradual, steady progress. The text says that seeking the great man brings success, that you need not fear, and that it is good to depart toward the south. Growth now is not sudden; it comes from patient effort and adaptation, like a plant bending around obstacles. Keep going, step by step.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward steady growth and gradual progress. Patient effort and good guidance will help you rise.
do: Make steady progress step by step
Seek guidance from those who can help
hexagrams.love: The relationship can grow gradually and steadily. Invest in it consistently.
hexagrams.work: Promotion or progress is possible through steady effort and good relationships with superiors.
hexagrams.self: Personal growth happens step by step. Celebrate small advances.
hexagrams.jung: Pushing Upward may describe the growth of consciousness from unconscious roots — gradual, organic and persistent.
hexagrams.example: Working your way up in a career, slowly improving a skill, or steadily recovering from illness.
hexagrams.judgment: Shăng indicates that (under its conditions) there will be great progress and success. Seeking by (the qualities implied in it) to meet with the great man, its subject need have no anxiety. Advance to the south will be fortunate.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) wood and that for the earth with the wood growing in the midst of it form Shăng. The superior man, in accordance with this, pays careful attention to his virtue, and accumulates the small developments of it till it is high and great.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject advancing upwards with the welcome (of those above him). There will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: Rising with the welcome and trust of those above you. Great good fortune.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject with that sincerity which will make even the (small) offerings of the vernal sacrifice acceptable. There will be no error.
lines.plain: When you are sincere, even a small offering is acceptable. Genuine intention matters more than outward show. No blame.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject ascending upwards (as into) an empty city.
lines.plain: Rising as if into an empty city. Nothing stands in your way now; go forward without hesitation.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject employed by the king to present his offerings on mount Khî. There will be good fortune; there will be no mistake.
lines.plain: Being honoured with a role on the sacred mountain. Faithful service is recognized. Good fortune and no blame.

lines.legge: The fifth six, divided, shows its subject firmly correct, and therefore enjoying good fortune. He ascends the stairs (with all due ceremony).
lines.plain: Firmness brings good fortune. Rise step by step, as one climbs stairs with dignity, rather than leaping ahead.

lines.legge: The sixth six, divided, shows its subject advancing upwards blindly. Advantage will be found in a ceaseless maintenance of firm correctness.
lines.plain: Rising in the dark, without seeing where you are going. Continue only with steady, unceasing correctness; blind ambition is dangerous.

hexagrams.name: Oppression
hexagrams.core: a time of hardship and exhaustion, when outer resources fail and inner integrity is what carries you through
hexagrams.now: A lake without water: it has drained away. Oppression describes a time of hardship, exhaustion or confinement. The text says it can still bring success to the great person who remains firm, and that words are not believed. Outer circumstances may be harsh, and explaining yourself may not help. What matters is inner integrity. The Image advises the superior person to stake their life on carrying out their will.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward difficulty or exhaustion. Inner strength and integrity will matter more than words or outer resources.
do: Hold on to your inner strength and values
Let actions speak instead of words
hexagrams.love: Difficult times can test a relationship. Stay steady and supportive without long arguments.
hexagrams.work: Resources may be scarce. Focus on what you can control and do not overpromise.
hexagrams.self: You may feel drained. Rest and remember what you stand for.
hexagrams.jung: Oppression may describe a state of psychic exhaustion when the conscious attitude has run dry. It can force a turn inward toward deeper sources of meaning.
hexagrams.example: Feeling burnt out at work, financial difficulties, or a period of loneliness.
hexagrams.judgment: In (the condition denoted by) Khwăn there may (yet be) progress and success. For the firm and correct, the (really) great man, there will be good fortune. He will fall into no error. If he make speeches, his words cannot be made good.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a marsh, and (below it that for a defile, which has drained the other dry so that there is) no water in it, form Khwăn. The superior man, in accordance with this, will sacrifice his life in order to carry out his purpose.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject with bare buttocks straitened under the stump of a tree. He enters a dark valley, and for three years has no prospect (of deliverance).
lines.plain: Sitting oppressed under a bare tree, wandering into a gloomy valley. You may see no way out for a long time. Do not sink deeper into despair; the darkness is not permanent.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject straitened amidst his wine and viands. There come to him anon the red knee-covers (of the ruler). It will be well for him (to maintain his sincerity as) in sacrificing. Active operations (on his part) will lead to evil, but he will be free from blame.
lines.plain: Oppressed even amid food and drink: comfort without fulfilment. Help from a person of rank is coming. Stay sincere as in a sacred rite; acting rashly now would bring trouble, though not blame.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject straitened before a (frowning) rock. He lays hold of thorns. He enters his palace, and does not see his wife. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Struggling against stone and grasping at thorns, returning home to find no one there. Fighting the wrong battles and leaning on what hurts you leads to misfortune.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided shows its subject proceeding very slowly (to help the subject of the first line), who is straitened by the carriage adorned with metal in front of him. There will be occasion for regret, but the end will be good.
lines.plain: Help comes slowly because it is blocked by obstacles that look impressive. There is embarrassment, but things come right in the end.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with his nose and feet cut off. He is straitened by (his ministers in their) scarlet aprons. He is leisurely in his movements, however, and is satisfied. It will be well for him to be (as sincere) as in sacrificing (to spiritual beings).
lines.plain: Hurt from above and below, oppressed by those in authority. Joy returns slowly. Remain sincere, as in an act of devotion.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject straitened, as if bound with creepers; or in a high and dangerous position, and saying (to himself), 'If I move, I shall repent it.' If he do repent of former errors, there will be good fortune in his going forward.
lines.plain: Tangled in creeping vines and anxious, telling yourself that any move will bring regret. If you recognize your past mistakes and act anyway, good fortune comes.

hexagrams.name: The Well
hexagrams.core: a time to return to a deep and lasting source, maintaining what nourishes everyone
hexagrams.now: Water above wood: the bucket rises from the well. The Well describes a source that remains constant while towns change around it. The text says the town may change, but the well cannot be changed; people come and go and draw from it. But if the rope is too short or the jug breaks, misfortune results. The well represents the deep resources that nourish life — human nature, shared wisdom, community. Make sure they are maintained and accessible.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a return to deeper sources of nourishment and wisdom. Maintaining and sharing them will be important.
hexagrams.love: Return to the shared source of your relationship: values, friendship and care.
hexagrams.work: Maintain systems and relationships that serve everyone. Invest in fundamentals.
hexagrams.self: Seek deeper sources of meaning and wisdom.
hexagrams.jung: The Well may symbolize the collective unconscious — the deep, shared source of images and meaning from which every individual draws.
hexagrams.example: Repairing community resources, returning to spiritual practice, or drawing on a mentor's deep wisdom.
hexagrams.judgment: (Looking at) Žing, (we think of) how (the site of) a town may be changed, while (the fashion of) its wells undergoes no change. (The water of a well) never disappears and never receives (any great) increase, and those who come and those who go can draw and enjoy the benefit. If (the drawing) have nearly been accomplished, but, before the rope has quite reached the water, the bucket is broken, this is evil.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) wood and above it that for water form Žing. The superior man, in accordance with this, comforts the people, and. stimulates them to mutual helpfulness.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows a well so muddy that men will not drink of it; or an old well to which neither birds (nor other creatures) resort.
lines.plain: The well is muddy and nobody drinks from it; even animals do not visit an old well. Neglected resources or skills become useless.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows a well from which by a hole the water escapes and flows away to the shrimps (and such small creatures among the grass), or one the water of which leaks away from a broken basket.
lines.plain: Water leaks from the well toward the small fish, or the jug is cracked and leaks. Your resources are being wasted on trivial things.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows a well, which has been cleared out, but is not used. Our hearts are sorry for this, for the water might be drawn out and used. If the king were (only) intelligent, both he and we might receive the benefit of it.
lines.plain: The well has been cleaned, but nobody drinks. This is a source of sadness. If those in authority recognized its value, everyone would benefit.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows a well, the lining of which is well laid. There will be no error.
lines.plain: The well is being lined with stone. Repairing and strengthening the source takes time, and no one is to blame for the pause.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows a clear, limpid well, (the waters from) whose cold spring are (freely) drunk.
lines.plain: The well holds clear, cold spring water that people can drink. Your resources are ready and valuable.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows (the water from) the well brought to the top, which is not allowed to be covered. This suggests the idea of sincerity. There will be great good fortune.
lines.plain: Water is drawn freely, and the well is left open for everyone. A dependable source, shared sincerely, brings great good fortune.

hexagrams.name: Revolution
hexagrams.core: a time of fundamental change, which succeeds when the moment is right and people trust the reason for it
hexagrams.now: Fire within the lake: two forces that cannot both stay as they are. Revolution describes a deep transformation, like an animal shedding its old coat. The traditional text says that people will believe in the change only "on the day of its completion", and that firm correctness makes regret disappear. Real change needs the right timing, a clear and fair purpose, and the trust of others. The Image advises the wise person to set the calendar in order and make the seasons clear — understand the rhythm of time before you overturn what exists.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a fundamental change. When the time is right and your motives are clear, transformation can bring renewal.
do: Make sure change is truly necessary and well-timed
Explain your reasons so others can trust them
Change what is outdated, keep what is sound
avoid: Changing things for the sake of change
Acting before you have support or clarity
hexagrams.love: The relationship may need to change its old patterns. Talk openly about what must be different, and change together.
hexagrams.work: Outdated structures or methods may need to be replaced. Prepare carefully and communicate clearly.
hexagrams.self: You may be ready to shed an old identity or habit. Let the new you emerge at a natural pace.
hexagrams.jung: Revolution can describe a fundamental shift in attitude, the kind of transformation Jung associated with the process of individuation, when an old way of being no longer fits and a new orientation emerges.
hexagrams.example: Changing careers, ending a habit that defined you, or transforming how a team or family works.
hexagrams.judgment: (What takes place as indicated by) Ko is believed in only after it has been accomplished. There will be great progress and success. Advantage will come from being firm and correct. (In that case) occasion for repentance will disappear.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing the waters of) a marsh and that for fire in the midst of them form Ko. The superior man, in accordance with this, regulates his (astronomical) calculations, and makes clear the seasons and times.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as if he were) bound with the skin of a yellow ox.
lines.plain: Wrapped in the hide of a yellow ox. It is too early to act. Hold firm and let the time for change mature.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject making his changes after some time has passed. Action taken will be fortunate. There will be no error.
lines.plain: When the day comes, carry out the change. The time is now right; going forward brings good fortune and no blame.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows that action taken by its subject will be evil. Though he be firm and correct, his position is perilous. If the change (he contemplates) have been three times fully discussed, he will be believed in.
lines.plain: Charging ahead brings misfortune, and stubbornness is dangerous. Only when talk of change has been considered three times does it deserve trust. Check your plans carefully.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows occasion for repentance disappearing (from its subject). Let him be believed in; and though he change (existing) ordinances, there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Regret disappears. People trust you, and changing the old order now brings good fortune. Sincerity gives the change its legitimacy.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the great man (producing his changes) as the tiger (does when he) changes (his stripes). Before he divines (and proceeds to action), faith has been reposed in him.
lines.plain: The great person changes like a tiger, whose stripes are clear and bright. The change is so evident that no oracle is needed; people trust it.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the superior man producing his changes as the leopard (does when he) changes (his spots), while small men change their faces (and show their obedience). To go forward (now) would lead to evil, but there will be good fortune in abiding firm and correct.
lines.plain: The superior person changes like a leopard, the petty person changes only their face. After the main change, do not keep pushing. Settling down and staying firm brings good fortune.

hexagrams.name: The Cauldron
hexagrams.core: a time of refinement and nourishing transformation, when raw materials become something of lasting value
hexagrams.now: Fire over wood: a sacred bronze cauldron in which food is cooked and offerings are prepared. The Cauldron is one of the few hexagrams that represents a man-made object, and it stands for culture, refinement and spiritual nourishment. The text promises supreme good fortune and success. Like cooking, transformation needs the right vessel, the right ingredients and the right heat. Put your gifts to good use and serve something larger than yourself.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward refinement and transformation, where raw potential becomes something nourishing and valuable.
do: Turn raw ideas or talents into something of value
Serve a purpose larger than yourself
avoid: Carrying more than the vessel can hold
hexagrams.love: Nourish the relationship with care, shared values and meaningful rituals.
hexagrams.work: Refine products, skills or teams into something of lasting value.
hexagrams.self: Your talents are being refined. Use them to nourish others.
hexagrams.jung: The Cauldron resembles the alchemical vessel, a symbol Jung used for the container in which psychological transformation happens. Raw emotion and experience are "cooked" into insight.
hexagrams.example: Developing a skill into a craft, preparing a meaningful meal or ceremony, or transforming experience into wisdom.
hexagrams.judgment: Ting gives the intimation of great progress and success.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) wood and above it that for fire form Ting. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps his every position correct, and maintains secure the appointment (of Heaven).

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows the caldron overthrown and its feet turned up. (But) there will be advantage in its getting rid of what was bad in it. (Or it shows us) the concubine (whose position is improved) by means of her son. There will be no error.
lines.plain: The cauldron is turned upside down to empty out old residue. Clearing away what is spoiled is helpful, even if it seems unusual. No blame.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with the things (to be cooked) in it. (If its subject can say), 'My enemy dislikes me, but he cannot approach me,' there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The cauldron has food in it. Others may envy you, but they cannot harm you. Keep your substance and stay focused. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with (the places of) its ears changed. The progress (of its subject) is (thus) stopped. The fat flesh of the pheasant (which is in the caldron) will not be eaten. But the (genial) rain will come, and the grounds for repentance will disappear. There will be good fortune in the end.
lines.plain: The handle of the cauldron is changed, so it cannot be lifted, and the good food is not eaten. Your gifts are not being used. Wait; when the rain comes, regret disappears and good fortune follows.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with its feet broken; and its contents, designed for the ruler's use, overturned and spilt. Its Subject will be made to blush for shame. There will be evil.
lines.plain: The cauldron's leg breaks and the prince's meal is spilled. Taking on more than you can handle leads to failure and embarrassment.

lines.legge: The fifth six, divided, shows the caldron with yellow ears and rings of metal in them. There will be advantage through being firm and correct.
lines.plain: The cauldron has yellow handles and golden carrying rings. You are open to help and good advice. Firmness brings benefit.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the caldron with rings of jade. There will be great good fortune, and all action taken will be in every way advantageous.
lines.plain: The cauldron has rings of jade. Great good fortune; everything is beneficial. Wisdom and gentleness are in harmony.

hexagrams.name: The Arousing
hexagrams.core: a sudden shock or upheaval that frightens at first but can awaken you and lead to composure and growth
hexagrams.now: Thunder repeated: a sudden shock. The Arousing describes events that startle and shake you. The traditional text describes the shock coming — "oh, oh!" — then laughter — "ha, ha!" — and says that even when the thunder terrifies for a hundred miles, the steady person does not drop the sacrificial spoon and cup. Shock can awaken you. The Image advises reflecting on yourself and setting your life in order. Fear passes; what remains is the lesson.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a shock or sudden change. Stay composed; it can awaken you to something important.
do: Use the shock to examine and correct yourself
Return to stability after the surprise
avoid: Ignoring the lesson of a shock
hexagrams.love: An unexpected event may shake the relationship. Stay steady and talk through what happened.
hexagrams.work: Sudden changes may occur. Keep composure and adapt quickly.
hexagrams.self: A shock can wake you up. Ask what it is showing you.
hexagrams.jung: The Arousing may describe a sudden irruption from the unconscious — an event, dream or emotion that shakes the ego out of complacency and opens it to change.
hexagrams.example: An unexpected job loss, a health scare, or sudden news that changes your perspective.
hexagrams.judgment: Kăn gives the intimation of ease and development. When (the time of) movement (which it indicates) comes, (the subject of the hexagram) will be found looking out with apprehension, and yet smiling and talking cheerfully. When the movement (like a crash of thunder) terrifies all within a hundred lî, he will be (like the sincere worshipper) who is not (startled into) letting go his ladle and (cup of) sacrificial spirits.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) thunder, being repeated, forms Kăn. The superior man, in accordance with this, is fearful and apprehensive, cultivates (his virtue), and examines (his faults).

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject, when the movement approaches, looking out and around with apprehension, and afterwards smiling and talking cheerfully. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Shock comes with fear and trembling, then laughter and relief. Good fortune follows the scare.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject, when the movement approaches, in a position of peril. He judges it better to let go the articles (in his possession), and to ascend a very lofty height. There is no occasion for him to pursue after (the things he has let go); in seven days he will find them.
lines.plain: Shock brings danger and you lose your treasures. Climb to higher ground and do not chase what is lost; in seven days it will return.

lines.legge: The third six, divided, shows its subject distraught amid the startling movements going on. If those movements excite him to (right) action, there will be no mistake.
lines.plain: Shock leaves you distraught. If shock moves you to act correctly, there is no harm.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject, amid the startling movements, supinely sinking (deeper) in the mud.
lines.plain: Shock leaves you stuck in the mud. Your energy is bogged down; you cannot respond well right now.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject going and coming amidst the startling movements (of the time), and always in peril; but perhaps he will not incur loss, and find business (which he can accomplish).
lines.plain: Shocks come and go, and danger surrounds you. Do not lose your center; there is still work to be done.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject, amidst the startling movements (of the time), in breathless dismay and looking round him with trembling apprehension. If he take action, there will be evil. If, while the startling movements have not reached his own person and his neighbourhood, (he were to take precautions), there would be no error, though his relatives might (still) speak against him.
lines.plain: Shock causes panic and wild looks. Going forward now brings misfortune. If the shock has not yet hit you but your neighbour, you can avoid harm. There may be gossip.

hexagrams.name: Keeping Still
hexagrams.core: a time of stillness, when calming the mind and stopping at the right moment brings clarity
hexagrams.now: Mountain upon mountain: stillness doubled. Keeping Still describes the art of rest and stopping. The text describes keeping the back still so that one no longer feels the body, and walking in the courtyard without noticing people — inner calm so deep that outer things no longer disturb. The Image advises the wise person not to let thoughts go beyond their situation. Stop when it is time to stop, move when it is time to move, and let the mind settle.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time of stillness. Calm reflection and knowing when to stop will matter more than action.
do: Pause and let your thoughts settle
avoid: Overthinking beyond what you can affect
hexagrams.love: Give each other space and quiet. Stillness can bring clarity.
hexagrams.work: Pause before big decisions. Rest prevents burnout.
hexagrams.self: A perfect time for meditation, retreat or rest.
hexagrams.jung: Keeping Still resembles meditation and the quieting of the ego so that the deeper Self can be perceived. Stillness allows unconscious contents to surface without being disturbed.
hexagrams.example: Taking a retreat, pausing a project to reflect, or learning to calm an anxious mind.
hexagrams.judgment: When one's resting is like that of the back, and he loses all consciousness of self; when he walks in his courtyard, and does not see any (of the persons) in it,--there will be no error.
hexagrams.image: (Two trigrams representing) a mountain, one over the other, form Kăn. The superior man, in 0 accordance with this, does not go in his thoughts beyond the (duties of the) position in which he is.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping his toes at rest. There will be no error; but it will be advantageous for him to be persistently firm and correct.
lines.plain: Keeping the toes still. Stopping before you even start prevents mistakes. Lasting firmness is beneficial.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping the calves of his legs at rest. He cannot help (the subject of the line above) whom he follows, and is dissatisfied in his mind.
lines.plain: Keeping the calves still. You cannot stop the person you follow, and your heart is not glad. You may have to go along with something you disagree with.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject keeping his loins at rest, and separating the ribs (from the body below). The situation is perilous, and the heart glows with suppressed excitement.
lines.plain: Keeping the hips still and stiffening the back. Forcing stillness creates tension and danger. True calm cannot be forced.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping his trunk at rest. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Keeping the trunk still. You have calmed yourself, even if you cannot yet calm others. No blame.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping his jawbones at rest, so that his words are (all) orderly. Occasion for repentance will disappear.
lines.plain: Keeping the jaws still. Speaking carefully and in order makes regret disappear.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows its subject devotedly maintaining his restfulness. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Noble-hearted stillness. A deep, settled calm brings good fortune.

hexagrams.name: Development
hexagrams.core: a time of gradual development, when lasting results come step by step, like a tree slowly growing on a mountain
hexagrams.now: A tree on a mountain grows slowly and stands firm. Development describes progress that happens in stages. The text uses the image of a maiden being given in marriage according to the proper customs — everything in its proper order. Rushing would undermine the result. Steady, patient progress builds something durable. The wild goose in the line texts flies step by step from the shore to the heights.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward slow, steady development. Patience and proper sequence will lead to lasting results.
do: Respect the proper order of things
hexagrams.love: Let the relationship develop naturally. Commitment grows through patience and respect.
hexagrams.work: Progress through careful stages. Lasting success takes time.
hexagrams.self: Personal growth happens gradually. Trust the process.
hexagrams.jung: Development describes the gradual process of individuation — the slow, organic growth of personality toward wholeness.
hexagrams.example: Building a career over years, a relationship deepening slowly, or learning a skill step by step.
hexagrams.judgment: Kien suggests to us the marriage of a young lady, and the good fortune (attending it). There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain and above it that for a tree form Kien. The superior man, in accordance with this, attains to and maintains his extraordinary virtue, and makes the manners of the people good.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows the wild geese gradually approaching the shore. A young officer (in similar circumstances) will be in a position of danger, and be spoken against; but there will be no error.
lines.plain: The wild goose gradually approaches the shore. A young person starting out may feel exposed and be criticised, but there is no real fault in moving forward carefully.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows the geese gradually approaching the large rocks, where they eat and drink joyfully and at ease. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The goose reaches a large rock. You have found a secure place; enjoy food and companionship in peace. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows them gradually advanced to the dry plains. (It suggests also the idea of) a husband who goes on an expedition from which he does not return, and of a wife who is pregnant, but will not nourish her child. There will be evil. (The case symbolised) might be advantageous in resisting plunderers.
lines.plain: The goose flies to the dry plateau, the wrong place for it. Pushing on too far leads to separation and disappointment. Instead, protect what you have against harm.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows the geese gradually advanced to the trees. They may light on the flat branches. There will be no error.
lines.plain: The goose lands in a tree, where it cannot easily stand. It may find a flat branch. Look for a safe, temporary position; there is no blame.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the geese gradually advanced to the high mound. (It suggests the idea of) a wife who for three years does not become pregnant; but in the end the natural issue cannot be prevented. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The goose reaches a high hill. Separation or delay may last a long time, but in the end nothing can prevent the good outcome. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the geese gradually advanced to the large heights (beyond). Their feathers can be used as ornaments. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The goose rises to the heights, and its feathers can be used for sacred dances. A life lived step by step becomes an example to others. Good fortune.

hexagrams.name: The Marrying Maiden
hexagrams.core: a situation in which you enter a relationship or role from a subordinate position, where tact and awareness of limits are essential
hexagrams.now: Thunder over the lake: the young woman follows the older man. The Marrying Maiden describes entering a relationship or situation from a subordinate position — as a secondary wife in ancient China. The traditional text warns that aggressive action brings misfortune and nothing furthers. This is not a time to demand or push. Understand your position, work within it with dignity, and keep the long term in mind. The Image advises understanding what will last by knowing what causes ruin.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a role where you have limited power. Patience, tact and dignity will be essential.
do: Understand your position and its limits
avoid: Entering commitments for the wrong reasons
hexagrams.love: Look honestly at the balance of power in the relationship. Commitments need to be fair to last.
hexagrams.work: You may be in a junior or dependent position. Work with dignity and make yourself valuable.
hexagrams.self: Notice where you feel subordinate or dependent. Accept limits while keeping self-respect.
hexagrams.jung: The Marrying Maiden may describe a relationship in which one person carries a projection that does not truly fit them. Psychological maturity requires recognizing the real person behind the projection.
hexagrams.example: Starting in a junior role, joining a family as an in-law, or accepting a partnership on unequal terms.
hexagrams.judgment: Kwei Mei indicates that (under the conditions which it denotes) action will be evil, and in no wise advantageous.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing the waters of) a marsh and over it that for thunder form Kwei Mei. The superior man, in accordance with this, having regard to the far-distant end, knows the mischief (that may be done at the beginning).

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows the younger sister married off in a position ancillary to the real wife. (It suggests the idea of) a person lame on one leg who yet manages to tramp along. Going forward will be fortunate.
lines.plain: Married as a junior wife: like a lame person who can still walk. A subordinate role can still be fulfilled with dignity, and moving forward brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows her blind of one eye, and yet able to see. There will be advantage in her maintaining the firm correctness of a solitary widow.
lines.plain: Like a one-eyed person who can still see. Even in a disappointing situation, stay loyal to your own inner standards, as a solitary person keeps faith.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows the younger sister who was to be married off in a mean position. She returns and accepts an ancillary position.
lines.plain: Expecting a high position, she must accept a lower one. Insisting on status you do not have leads nowhere; accept the real situation and rebuild from there.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the younger sister who is to be married off protracting the time. She may be late in being married, but the time will come.
lines.plain: The marriage is delayed past its expected time. Waiting for the right partner or moment is wise; it will come later.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, reminds us of the marrying of the younger sister of (king) Tî-yî, when the sleeves of her the princess were not equal to those of the (still) younger sister who accompanied her in an inferior capacity. (The case suggests the thought of) the moon almost full. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The king's daughter wears plainer clothes than her bridesmaid. Modesty and inner worth matter more than outward display. Like the moon nearly full, she shines without needing to show off. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided, shows the young lady bearing the basket, but without anything in it, and the gentleman slaughtering the sheep, but without blood flowing from it. There will be no advantage in any way.
lines.plain: A woman holds a basket with no fruit, and a man sacrifices a sheep without blood. Going through the motions of a commitment without real substance brings no benefit.

hexagrams.name: Abundance
hexagrams.core: a peak of abundance and achievement, which should be used fully and wisely because it will not last forever
hexagrams.now: Thunder and lightning arrive together: a moment of brilliant fullness. Abundance describes a peak — of success, energy or influence. The text says the king attains abundance and should not be sad; be like the sun at midday. Enjoy and use this fullness, but remember that the sun at its height begins to decline. The Image advises deciding lawsuits and carrying out punishments — that is, making clear, decisive judgments while you have the clarity to do so.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a peak of abundance. Use it wisely and decisively, knowing it will not last.
do: Make the most of this peak
hexagrams.love: Celebrate what you have together. Make decisions you have been postponing.
hexagrams.work: A peak period. Complete important tasks and make clear decisions.
hexagrams.self: Enjoy your energy and clarity, but prepare for quieter times.
hexagrams.jung: Abundance may describe a peak of conscious energy and clarity — a moment of fullness that carries the seeds of its own decline.
hexagrams.example: A successful season in business, a celebration, or a peak in personal achievement.
hexagrams.judgment: Făng intimates progress and development. When a king has reached the point (which the name denotes) there is no occasion to be anxious (through fear of a change). Let him be as the sun at noon.
hexagrams.image: (The trigrams representing) thunder and lightning combine to form Făng. The superior man, in accordance with this, decides cases of litigation, and apportions punishments with exactness.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject meeting with his mate. Though they are both of the same character, there will be no error. Advance will call forth approval.
lines.plain: You meet a partner who matches you. Even if you are alike, working together for a while is not a mistake, and moving forward wins recognition.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject surrounded by screens so large and thick that at midday he can see from them the constellation of the Bushel. If he go (and try to enlighten his ruler who is thus emblemed), he will make himself to be viewed with suspicion and dislike. Let him cherish his feeling of sincere devotion that he may thereby move (his ruler's mind), and there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: A curtain so thick that stars are visible at noon. Your clarity is hidden by those above you. Trying to force your views would create suspicion; sincere patience will eventually win trust.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject with an (additional) screen of a large and thick banner, through which at midday he can see (the small) Mei star. (In the darkness) he breaks his right arm; but there will be no error.
lines.plain: The darkness thickens, and you break your right arm. You may be unable to act for now. That is not your fault.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject in a tent so large and thick that at midday he can see from it the constellation of the Bushel. But he meets with the subject of the (first) line, undivided like himself. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: The curtain is thick and the light is obscured, but you meet a like-minded ally. Working together brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject bringing around him the men of brilliant ability. There will be occasion for congratulation and praise. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: You bring talented people around you. Recognition and good fortune follow from gathering bright minds.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with his house made large, but only serving as a screen to his household. When he looks at his door, it is still, and there is nobody about it. For three years no one is to be seen. There will be evil.
lines.plain: A great house that shuts out the world. Looking through the door, you see no one. Isolation at the height of abundance leads to long loneliness and misfortune.

hexagrams.name: The Wanderer
hexagrams.core: a time of travel or transition, when caution, modesty and adaptability keep you safe in unfamiliar places
hexagrams.now: Fire on the mountain: it burns briefly and moves on. The Wanderer describes being a stranger — travelling, in transition or in an unfamiliar situation. The text says success comes in small matters; firmness and correctness bring good fortune to the traveller. As a stranger, you have no established position. Be cautious, modest and adaptable. The Image advises the wise person to be clear-minded and careful in imposing penalties, and not to drag out lawsuits.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a period of transition or unfamiliar territory. Caution, modesty and adaptability will help.
hexagrams.love: A relationship may feel temporary or uncertain. Be respectful and honest about where you stand.
hexagrams.work: You may be new or temporary in a role. Learn the culture and avoid conflicts.
hexagrams.self: You may feel like a stranger to yourself. Explore with curiosity.
hexagrams.jung: The Wanderer may describe the psychological state of being between identities — no longer who you were and not yet who you will be. The journey itself is transformative.
hexagrams.example: Moving to a new country, starting a temporary job, or travelling alone.
hexagrams.judgment: Lü intimates that (in the condition which it denotes) there may be some little attainment and progress. If the stranger or traveller be firm and correct as he ought to be, there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a mountain and above it that for fire form Lü. The superior man, in accordance with this, exerts his wisdom and caution in the use of punishments and not allowing litigations to continue.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows the stranger mean and meanly occupied. It is thus that he brings on himself (further) calamity.
lines.plain: A traveller who occupies himself with petty matters brings trouble on himself. Keep your dignity even when you are a stranger.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows the stranger, occupying his lodging-house, carrying with him his means of livelihood, and provided with good and trusty servants.
lines.plain: The traveller finds lodging, keeps his resources with him and wins a faithful helper. Prudence and modesty make a stranger safe.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows the stranger, burning his lodging-house, and having lost his servants. However firm and correct he (try to) be, he will be in peril.
lines.plain: The traveller's lodging burns, and he loses his helper's loyalty through arrogance. Pride in an unfamiliar place is dangerous.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows the traveller in a resting-place, having (also) the means of livelihood and the axe, (but still saying), 'I am not at ease in my mind.'
lines.plain: The traveller has found shelter, resources and protection, but his heart is not at ease. Outward security does not end the feeling of being a stranger.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject shooting a pheasant. He will lose his arrow, but in the end he will obtain praise and a (high) charge.
lines.plain: Shooting a pheasant and losing an arrow. A small sacrifice opens the door to recognition and a respected role.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, suggests the idea of a bird burning its nest. The stranger, (thus represented), first laughs and then cries out. He has lost his ox(-like docility) too readily and easily. There will be evil.
lines.plain: A bird's nest burns. The traveller laughs at first, then weeps, having lost his patience and gentleness too easily. Carelessness and arrogance bring misfortune.

hexagrams.name: The Gentle
hexagrams.core: a time when gentle, persistent influence achieves more than force, like wind that penetrates everywhere
hexagrams.now: Wind following wind: gentle penetration. The Gentle describes influence that works slowly and persistently, like wind that shapes trees or water that wears down stone. The text says small successes come, that it is good to have somewhere to go and to see the great man. The Image advises the wise person to repeat their instructions and carry out their affairs — clear, repeated communication works best. Be gentle, but know exactly what you want.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time when gentle, persistent influence is the most effective approach.
hexagrams.love: Gentle words and persistence can heal tensions. Be clear about what you want.
hexagrams.work: Persuade through repeated, clear communication. Small steps will add up.
hexagrams.self: Change your habits gently and consistently.
hexagrams.jung: The Gentle may describe the subtle influence of the unconscious, which works quietly and persistently on the conscious mind, often through intuition and recurring images.
hexagrams.example: Gradually persuading a team, influencing a child's habits, or slowly changing a long-standing pattern.
hexagrams.judgment: Sun intimates that (under the conditions which it denotes) there will be some little attainment and progress. There will be advantage in movement onward in whatever direction. It will be advantageous (also) to see the great man.
hexagrams.image: (Two trigrams representing) wind, following each other, form Sun. The superior man, in accordance with this, reiterates his orders, and secures the practice of his affairs.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject (now) advancing, (now) receding. It would be advantageous for him to have the firm correctness of a brave soldier.
lines.plain: Moving forward and back in indecision. Doubt keeps you from acting. Adopt the firm discipline of a soldier: decide and commit.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows the representative of Sun beneath a couch, and employing diviners and exorcists in a way bordering on confusion. There will be good fortune and no error.
lines.plain: Penetration under the bed. Hidden influences need to be brought to light, and it may take the help of specialists or even ritual. With persistence, good fortune and no blame.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject penetrating (only) by violent and repeated efforts. There will be occasion for regret.
lines.plain: Repeated penetration. Constantly changing your mind, or forcing gentleness too often, leads to humiliation.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows all occasion for repentance (in its subject) passed away. He takes game for its threefold use in his hunting.
lines.plain: Remorse disappears. During the hunt, three kinds of game are caught. Gentle, well-directed effort brings rich results.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows that with firm correctness there will be good fortune (to its subject). All occasion for repentance will disappear, and all his movements will be advantageous. There may have been no (good) beginning, but there will be a (good) end. Three days before making any changes, (let him give notice of them); and three days after, (let him reconsider them). There will (thus) be good fortune.
lines.plain: Firmness brings good fortune, and remorse disappears. Nothing is without benefit. Without a good beginning there can still be a good end: consider carefully before and after a change.

lines.legge: The sixth NINE, undivided, shows the representative of penetration beneath a couch, and having lost the axe with which he executed his decisions. However firm and correct he may (try to) be, there will be evil.
lines.plain: Penetration under the bed, losing your property and your axe. Going too far in gentleness or submission costs you your means of defense. Persistence here brings misfortune.

hexagrams.name: The Joyous
hexagrams.core: a time of joy and open communication, when sincere pleasure shared with others brings success
hexagrams.now: Two lakes connected: water flows between them. The Joyous describes joy, pleasure and open communication. The text promises success to those who are firm and correct. True joy comes from within and is shared with others; it does not depend on outside excitement. The Image advises the wise person to join with friends for discussion and practice. Enjoy and share, but make sure the joy is sincere and not based on flattery or indulgence.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward joy and open communication. Sincere sharing with others will strengthen bonds.
hexagrams.love: Joy, laughter and honest conversation deepen love now.
hexagrams.work: A positive atmosphere helps teamwork. Encourage open discussion.
hexagrams.self: Notice what genuinely brings you joy.
hexagrams.jung: The Joyous may describe the life-affirming energy of eros and connection. Psychologically, joy shared with others can integrate the personality, while compulsive pleasure-seeking can mask emptiness.
hexagrams.example: Celebrating with friends, a lively discussion, or the joy of learning something new together.
hexagrams.judgment: Tui intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and attainment. (But) it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: (Two symbols representing) the waters of a marsh, one over the other, form Tui. The superior man, in accordance with this, (encourages) the conversation of friends and (the stimulus of) their (common) practice.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows the pleasure of (inward) harmony. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Joy that comes from inner harmony, not from outside things. Contentment of this kind brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows the pleasure arising from (inward) sincerity. There will be good fortune. Occasion for repentance will disappear.
lines.plain: Joy rooted in sincerity and trust. Good fortune; regret disappears.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject bringing round himself whatever can give pleasure. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Joy that comes from chasing pleasures from outside yourself. Seeking constant stimulation leaves you empty and leads to trouble.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject deliberating about what to seek his pleasure in, and not at rest. He borders on what would be injurious, but there will be cause for joy.
lines.plain: You are weighing which kind of pleasure to choose and are not at peace. If you turn away from what harms you, real joy will come.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject trusting in one who would injure him. The situation is perilous.
lines.plain: Trusting someone or something that undermines you. Even pleasant influences can be harmful. Be careful.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows the pleasure of its subject in leading and attracting others.
lines.plain: Being drawn along by the pull of pleasure, without direction of your own. Notice where you are being led.

hexagrams.name: Dispersion
hexagrams.core: a time to dissolve rigid barriers and scattered energies, bringing people back together around a shared purpose
hexagrams.now: Wind blows over the water and disperses it. Dispersion describes the dissolving of what is rigid or blocked — tensions, egotism or separation. The text says the king approaches his temple and that crossing the great water is beneficial. Dissolving barriers can unite people again around something larger. The Image describes ancient kings sacrificing to the Lord and building temples. Spiritual or shared purpose can overcome division.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time when rigid barriers dissolve and people can unite around shared purpose.
do: Unite people around a shared purpose
hexagrams.love: Let go of pride and resentment. Reconnect through shared values.
hexagrams.work: Break down silos and unite the team around a common purpose.
hexagrams.self: Release rigid attitudes or emotional blockages.
hexagrams.jung: Dispersion may describe the dissolving of rigid ego-boundaries. It can open space for new connections with the unconscious and with others.
hexagrams.example: Resolving a family feud, breaking down barriers between departments, or letting go of an old grudge.
hexagrams.judgment: Hwân intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and success. The king goes to his ancestral temple; and it will be advantageous to cross the great stream. It will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) water and that for wind moving above the water form Hwân. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, presented offerings to God and established the ancestral temple.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject engaged in rescuing (from the impending evil) and having (the assistance of) a strong horse. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Bringing help with the strength of a horse. Acting quickly at the first sign of division prevents things from scattering. Good fortune.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject, amid the dispersion, hurrying to his contrivance (for security). All occasion for repentance will disappear.
lines.plain: As things scatter, you hurry to what can support you. Finding stable ground makes regret disappear.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject discarding any regard to his own person. There will be no occasion for repentance.
lines.plain: Letting go of concern for yourself. Dissolving selfishness frees you to serve something larger. No regret.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject scattering the (different) parties (in the state); which leads to great good fortune. From the dispersion (he collects again good men standing out, a crowd) like a mound, which is what ordinary men would not have thought of.
lines.plain: Breaking up narrow factions so that a larger unity can form. This brings great good fortune; ordinary people could not imagine such a gathering.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject amidst the dispersion issuing his great announcements as the perspiration (flows from his body). He scatters abroad (also) the accumulations in the royal granaries. There will be no error.
lines.plain: In the midst of dispersion, a leader speaks with great conviction, like sweat pouring out, and shares resources widely. Generosity and clear communication bring everyone together. No blame.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject disposing of (what may be called) its bloody wounds, and going and separating himself from its anxious fears. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Removing yourself and others from danger and harm. Keeping your distance from what threatens bloodshed is no mistake.

hexagrams.name: Limitation
hexagrams.core: a time to set wise limits and boundaries, which give structure and freedom when they are not too harsh
hexagrams.now: Water above the lake: a lake can hold only so much. Limitation describes the boundaries that give life structure. The text says limitation brings success, but harsh limitation should not be persisted in. Healthy limits — on spending, time, energy, commitments — create freedom. The Image advises creating number and measure and examining the nature of virtue and correct conduct. Limits should be wise and bearable.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a need for limits. Sensible boundaries will help, but avoid being too harsh.
hexagrams.love: Healthy boundaries make the relationship stronger. Respect each other's limits.
hexagrams.work: Set budgets, schedules and boundaries. Do not overextend.
hexagrams.self: Know your limits and respect them.
hexagrams.jung: Limitation may describe the necessary boundaries of the ego, which allow it to function without being flooded by unconscious contents.
hexagrams.example: Creating a budget, setting working hours, or establishing boundaries with demanding people.
hexagrams.judgment: Kieh intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and attainment. (But) if the regulations (which it prescribes) be severe and difficult, they cannot be permanent.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a lake, and above it that for water, form Kieh. The superior man, in accordance with this, constructs his (methods of) numbering and measurement, and discusses (points of) virtue and conduct.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject not quitting the courtyard outside his door. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Not going out beyond your own courtyard. Knowing when to stay quiet and stay put is no mistake.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject not quitting the courtyard inside his gate. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Not going beyond your own gate when the time to act has come. Holding back too long brings misfortune.

lines.legge: . The third SIX, divided, shows its subject with no appearance of observing the (proper) regulations, in which case we shall see him lamenting. But there will be no one to blame (but himself).
lines.plain: Ignoring all limits brings regret and lament. There is no one to blame but yourself.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject quietly and naturally (attentive to all) regulations. There will be progress and success.
lines.plain: Accepting limits peacefully and naturally. Calm self-discipline brings success.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject sweetly and acceptably enacting his regulations. There will be good fortune. The onward progress with them will afford ground for admiration.
lines.plain: Limits that are pleasant and accepted. Leading by example with fair rules brings good fortune and respect.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject enacting regulations severe and difficult. Even with firmness and correctness there will be evil. But though there will be cause for repentance, it will (by and by) disappear.
lines.plain: Harsh and bitter limits. Insisting on them brings misfortune, although regret will pass when you soften.

hexagrams.name: Inner Truth
hexagrams.core: a time when sincerity and inner truth create trust strong enough to move even the most difficult hearts
hexagrams.now: Wind blows over the lake, stirring the water. Inner Truth describes sincerity so deep that it influences even pigs and fishes — the least responsive creatures. The text says it brings good fortune and that crossing the great water is beneficial. Real influence comes from truthful inner attitude. The Image advises the wise person to discuss criminal cases thoughtfully and delay executions — sincerity combined with understanding and mercy.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time when sincerity and inner truth create trust and influence.
hexagrams.love: Honesty and empathy build deep trust. Speak from the heart.
hexagrams.work: Trust within the team is crucial. Be sincere and transparent.
hexagrams.self: Connect with your inner truth.
