hexagrams.jung: Inner Truth may describe the connection between the ego and the Self — the inner center that provides genuine orientation and integrity.
hexagrams.example: Building trust in a new relationship, mediating a conflict, or acting on your deepest convictions.
hexagrams.judgment: Kung Fû (moves even) pigs and fish, and leads to good fortune. There will be advantage in crossing the great stream. There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing the waters of) a marsh and that for wind above it form Kung Fû. The superior man, in accordance with this, deliberates about cases of litigation and delays (the infliction of) death.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject resting (in himself). There will be good fortune. If he sought to any other, he would not find rest.
lines.plain: Being prepared and resting in yourself brings good fortune. If you look for security from others or follow hidden motives, you lose your peace.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject (like) the crane crying out in her hidden retirement, and her young ones responding to her. (It is as if it were said), 'I have a cup of good spirits,' (and the response were), 'I will partake of it with you.'
lines.plain: A crane calls from the shade, and its young answer. "I have a good cup; I will share it with you." Sincere feeling finds an echo even at a distance.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject having met with his mate. Now he beats his drum, and now he leaves off. Now he weeps, and now he sings.
lines.plain: Finding a companion, but swinging between beating the drum and stopping, weeping and singing. Depending on others for your mood makes you unstable.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject (like) the moon nearly full, and (like) a horse (in a chariot) whose fellow disappears. There will be no error.
lines.plain: The moon is almost full; one horse of a pair goes its own way. Turn toward what is higher, even if it means leaving a companion. No blame.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject perfectly sincere, and linking (others) to him in closest union. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Sincerity that links people together. Genuine trust in leadership brings no blame.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject in chanticleer (trying to) mount to heaven. Even with firm correctness there will be evil.
lines.plain: A rooster trying to fly up to heaven. Grand words without inner substance. Persisting in this brings misfortune.

hexagrams.name: Preponderance of the Small
hexagrams.core: a time when small matters and careful conduct are more important than great undertakings
hexagrams.now: Thunder on the mountain: a sound that does not travel far. Preponderance of the Small describes a time when small things matter more than great ambitions. The text says success comes in small matters, not great ones. A flying bird brings a message: it is not good to strive upward; it is good to stay below. Be modest, careful and attentive to detail. The Image advises excess in reverence, mourning and thrift.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a time when careful attention to small matters is more important than great ambitions.
hexagrams.love: Small gestures of care matter more than grand declarations.
hexagrams.work: Avoid big risks. Focus on details and small improvements.
hexagrams.self: Take small, careful steps.
hexagrams.jung: Preponderance of the Small may describe the importance of small, overlooked details — the minor symptoms or slips that reveal what the unconscious is trying to communicate.
hexagrams.example: Double-checking work, being careful in a delicate situation, or focusing on small daily habits.
hexagrams.judgment: Hsiâo Kwo indicates that (in the circumstances which it implies) there will be progress and attainment. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. (What the name denotes) may be done in small affairs, but not in great affairs. (It is like) the notes that come down from a bird on the wing;--to descend is better than to ascend. There will (in this way) be great good fortune.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) a hill and that for thunder above it form Hsiâo Kwo. The superior man, in accordance with this, in his conduct exceeds in humility, in mourning exceeds in sorrow, and in his expenditure exceeds in economy.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, suggests (the idea of) a bird flying, (and ascending) till the issue is evil.
lines.plain: A bird that flies too high meets with misfortune. Do not overreach; stay close to the ground for now.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject passing by his grandfather, and meeting with his grandmother; not attempting anything against his ruler, but meeting him as his minister. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Passing by the grandfather and meeting the grandmother; not reaching the ruler but meeting his minister. Accept a modest role and the appropriate channel. No blame.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject taking no extraordinary precautions against danger; and some in consequence finding opportunity to assail and injure him. There will be evil.
lines.plain: Not taking special precautions can lead to someone attacking from behind. Be extra careful now; small oversights can cause big harm.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject falling into no error, but meeting (the exigency of his situation), without exceeding (in his natural course). If he go forward, there will be peril, and he must be cautious. There is no occasion to be using firmness perpetually.
lines.plain: No blame. Meet the situation as it is without going beyond it. Going forward is dangerous; be careful and do not insist stubbornly.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, (suggests the idea) of dense clouds, but no rain, coming from our borders in the west. It also (shows) the prince shooting his arrow, and taking the bird in a cave.
lines.plain: Dense clouds but no rain from the west. The prince shoots and takes the bird in its cave. You cannot accomplish everything now, but you can find capable helpers.

lines.legge: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject not meeting (the exigency of his situation), and exceeding (his proper course). (It suggests the idea of) a bird flying far aloft. There will be evil. The case is what is called one of calamity and self-produced injury.
lines.plain: Flying too high and passing the goal. Going beyond what is right brings misfortune and self-inflicted harm.

hexagrams.name: After Completion
hexagrams.core: a time after completion, when everything seems in order but continued care is needed to prevent decline
hexagrams.now: Water over fire: everything is in its proper place. After Completion describes a moment when a goal has been reached and order established. The text says success in small matters, and warns: at the beginning good fortune, at the end disorder. When things are complete, the danger is complacency. The Image advises the wise person to think of misfortune and take precautions in advance. Maintain what you have achieved.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward completion. Stay vigilant and maintain what you have achieved.
hexagrams.love: The relationship may feel settled. Keep nurturing it so that it stays alive.
hexagrams.work: A project has been completed. Now focus on maintenance and quality.
hexagrams.self: Celebrate your achievement, but do not stop growing.
hexagrams.jung: After Completion may describe a state of psychological balance that, like all states, is temporary. The psyche is always in motion, and stability must be renewed.
hexagrams.example: Finishing a degree, completing a major project, or reaching a long-sought goal.
hexagrams.judgment: Kî Žî intimates progress and success in small matters. There will be advantage in being firm and correct. There has been good fortune in the beginning; there may be disorder in the end.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) fire and that for water above it form Kî Žî. The superior man, in accordance with this, thinks of evil (that may come), and beforehand guards against it.

lines.legge: The first NINE, undivided, (shows its subject as a driver) who drags back his wheel, (or as a fox) which has wet his tail. There will be no error.
lines.plain: Braking the wheels; the fox gets its tail wet. Slowing down at the start of a new phase prevents greater trouble. No blame.

lines.legge: The second SIX, divided, (shows its subject as) a wife who has lost her (carriage-)screen. There is no occasion to go in pursuit of it. In seven days she will find it.
lines.plain: A woman loses the curtain of her carriage. Do not chase what is lost; in seven days it will return by itself.

lines.legge: The third NINE, undivided, (suggests the case of) Kâo Žung, who attacked the Demon region, but was three years in subduing it. Small men should not be employed (in such enterprises).
lines.plain: A long campaign against a distant land takes three years. Great tasks after a success are exhausting. Do not give responsibility to petty people.

lines.legge: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject with rags provided against any leak (in his boat), and on his guard all day long.
lines.plain: Even the finest garments can turn to rags; a leaking boat needs patching. Stay alert all day to avoid disaster.

lines.legge: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject (as) the neighbour in the east who slaughters an ox (for his sacrifice); but this is not equal to the (small) spring sacrifice of the neighbour in the west, whose sincerity receives the blessing.
lines.plain: A neighbour who sacrifices an ox gains less than one who makes a small, sincere offering. Sincerity counts more than show.

lines.legge: The topmost SIX, divided, shows its subject with (even) his head immersed. The position is perilous.
lines.plain: Getting your head wet as you cross. Overconfidence at the end brings danger.

hexagrams.name: Before Completion
hexagrams.core: a time just before completion, when caution and careful discernment can still bring success
hexagrams.now: Fire over water: nothing is yet in its proper place. Before Completion is the final hexagram, but it describes a situation that is not yet complete. The text pictures a little fox that has almost crossed the river but gets its tail wet. Success is possible, but only with great care. Separate things carefully and put each in its place. The transition is not yet finished; do not relax too early.
hexagrams.dir: The situation may be moving toward a transition that is not yet complete. Careful discernment and patience will help you finish well.
do: Proceed carefully through the final steps
Sort things out and put them in order
hexagrams.love: The relationship is still developing. Do not take anything for granted.
hexagrams.work: The project is almost done but not finished. Pay attention to the final details.
hexagrams.self: You are in transition. Be patient and careful as you complete it.
hexagrams.jung: Before Completion may describe the ongoing nature of psychological development: individuation is never finished. Each completion opens a new beginning.
hexagrams.example: The final stage of a long project, the last months of a degree, or the period just before a major life change.
hexagrams.judgment: Wei Žî intimates progress and success (in the circumstances which it implies). (We see) a young fox that has nearly crossed (the stream), when its tail gets immersed. There will be no advantage in any way.
hexagrams.image: (The trigram representing) water and that for fire above it form Wei Žî. The superior man, in accordance with this, carefully discriminates among (the qualities of) things, and the (different) positions they (naturally) occupy.

lines.legge: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject (like a fox) whose tail gets immersed. There will be occasion for regret.
lines.plain: Getting your tail wet. Rushing ahead before you are ready brings embarrassment.

lines.legge: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject dragging back his (carriage-) wheel. With firmness and correctness there will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Braking the wheels. Holding back and waiting for the right time brings good fortune.

lines.legge: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject, with (the state of things) not yet remedied, advancing on; which will lead to evil. But there will be advantage in (trying to) cross the great stream.
lines.plain: Before completion, attacking now brings misfortune. Instead, it is good to make a larger journey to reach new conditions.

lines.legge: The fourth NINE, undivided, shows its subject by firm correctness obtaining good fortune, so that all occasion for repentance disappears. Let him stir himself up, as if he were invading the Demon region, where for three years rewards will come to him (and his troops) from the great kingdom.
lines.plain: Steady correctness brings good fortune and regret disappears. Determined effort over a long time, like a three-year campaign, is rewarded.

lines.legge: The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject by firm correctness obtaining good fortune, and having no occasion for repentance. (We see in him) the brightness of a superior man, and the possession of sincerity. There will be good fortune.
lines.plain: Steady correctness brings good fortune without regret. The light of a good person shines with sincerity.

lines.legge: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject full of confidence and therefore feasting (quietly). There will be no error. (If he) cherish this confidence, till he (is like the fox who) gets his head immersed, it will fail of what is right.
lines.plain: Celebrating with confidence and trust is fine. But if you overindulge and lose your head, you lose what you have gained.
